ACACIA.ritualUses: 在印度，這種木材被用作聖火的燃料，也用於建造神廟。
ACACIA.magicalUses: 將樹枝放在床上可避邪,在東方國家,會將其捲在頭巾內,也是 基於一様的道理。與檀木一起燃燒時,會激發出其靈力。在金錢和愛情的咒 語中也會用到阿拉伯膠樹,但在後者中，僅會得到柏拉圖式的愛情。
ACACIA.lore: Sacred to ancient Egyptians as a symbol of the afterlife; the Ark of the Covenant was said to be built of acacia wood.

ADAM.magicalUses: 在一小袋子中放入兩條根隨身攜帶,可吸引新戀情。若是想要擺 脱強勁的情敵,也可將這藥草的兩條根縫在小袋子裡,随身攜帶。送給一對
ADAM.lore: Named for their paired tubers resembling male and female forms, these orchid roots are central to Hoodoo love magic traditions.

ADDER'S.magicalUses: 將一些艾德之舌浸泡在冷水中,然後將其塗抹在傷口或瘀青上 (以一塊布包裹起來),直到藥草變暖。接下來,將濕藥草埋進泥濘的土地
ADDER'S.lore: Medieval herbalists believed this fern's spore-bearing frond resembled a snake's tongue, linking it to healing serpent lore.

AFRICAN.magicalUses: 在家中種植這種紫色花朵和植物,能提升住家的靈性。這種植物
AFRICAN.lore: Discovered in 1892 in Tanzania, this popular houseplant became associated with spiritual protection in modern witchcraft.

AGARIC.ritualUses: 據推測,至少有一些古典時代的神秘宗教在舉行秘密儀式時,主 要使用的藥草就是毒蠅傘。
AGARIC.magicalUses: 放在祭壇上或臥室裡,可以增加生育能力。不幸的是,毒蠅傘的
AGARIC.lore: Ancient Siberian shamans used this red-and-white mushroom in vision quests; some scholars link it to the Vedic divine drink Soma.

AGRIMONY.magicalUses: 可用於所有保護型的香包和法術,也能消除負能量和邪靈。它可 以抵抗地精、邪恶和毒藥。
AGRIMONY.lore: Anglo-Saxon healers listed agrimony in the Nine Herbs Charm; medieval legend says it could make the sleeping impossible to wake.

AGUE.magicalUses: 撒在家裡,可防止邪惡入侵,放在香包中,亦有同樣的效果。此
AGUE.lore: Native American peoples used this stargrass as protective medicine; its name reflects its historical use against malarial fevers.

ALFALFA.magicalUses: 放在家中可以避免陷入貧困和飢餓。最好放在櫥櫃或餐具室的小 罐子中。此外,將紫花苜蓿燒成灰燼,撒在房子周圍,也有同樣的效果。紫
ALFALFA.lore: One of the oldest cultivated crops, grown in ancient Persia over 3,000 years ago; Arabic traders named it 'the father of all foods.'

ALKANET.magicalUses: 將染色朱草當成薰香來燒,可淨化負面的領域,也用來促成各種
ALKANET.lore: Used since antiquity as a natural red dye; ancient Egyptians colored cosmetics and fabrics with its root pigment.

ALLSPICE.magicalUses: 將多香果當成薰香來燒香,可招財或增添好運,也會加到這類魔
ALLSPICE.lore: The Mayans used allspice to embalm their dead; Columbus brought it to Europe thinking he had found pepper, hence the name.

ALMOND.magicalUses: 杏仁的果實、葉子和木材可用於發達和金錢法術。此外，據説爬 杏仁樹可確保商業投資的成功。
ALMOND.lore: In Greek myth, the almond tree sprang from the blood of the goddess Cybele; it symbolizes divine favor and hidden wisdom.

ALOE.magicalUses: 蘆薈是一種常見的室內植物,也具有保護作用。可以驅邪,並預 防家庭事故。在非洲,人們會將蘆薈懸掛在房屋和門上,藉以趨吉避凶。
ALOE.lore: Cleopatra reportedly used aloe in her beauty rituals; Alexander the Great conquered Socotra island to secure its aloe supply for healing soldiers.

ALOES,WOOD.magicalUses: 在經過很長一段不易取得的時期後,今日沉香的取得變得日益普 遍。在魔法歷史中，已經使用沉香好幾個世紀,因此将其納入本書中。
ALOES,WOOD.lore: Mentioned in the Bible and Quran; ancient traders valued aloeswood (agarwood) more than gold for its heavenly fragrance.

ALTHEA.magicalUses: 藥蜀葵長期以來一直都用在保護儀式中，也是一種很好的靈力誘 發劑。要達到這種效果,可將其當成薰香來燒,或是製成香包隨身攜帶。
ALTHEA.lore: The 'marshmallow' plant — ancient Romans ate its roots as a delicacy, and its mucilage was the original base for marshmallow candy.

ALYSSUM.magicalUses: 古羅馬《藥物論》作者迪奧斯克里 德斯( Dioscorides) 建議將庭薺當作護身符,因 為它具有「破除魔咒」的能力。掛在房子裸能防止迷戀,這種魔法過程也稱
ALYSSUM.lore: Its name comes from Greek 'a-lyssa' meaning 'without madness'; ancients believed it could cure rabies and calm anger.

AMARANTH.ritualUses: 千穗谷用於異教徒的埋葬儀式。曾被墨西哥的西班牙殖民官所禁 用,因為阿茲特克人會使用在他們的儀式中。
AMARANTH.magicalUses: 將千穗谷做成的花冠戴在頭上,可加速療癒。要確保不會遭槍彈 擊中,最好是在满月的星期五时拔起整棵千穗谷(包括根部)。向這株植物 獻上祭品,然後用一塊白布將全株(含折疊起來的根部)包裹起來,並戴在 胸前，就可「防彈」。
AMARANTH.lore: The Aztecs mixed amaranth with honey and human blood for religious ceremonies; the Spanish conquistadors banned its cultivation.

ANEMONE.magicalUses: 春天第一次看到時,採集其花朵,用紅布包起來,穿戴或攜帶在 身上,可預防疾病。在花園裡種植紅色的歐洲白頭翁,可以同時保護花園和
ANEMONE.lore: In Greek myth, anemones sprang from Aphrodite's tears over the slain Adonis; their name means 'daughter of the wind.'

ANGELICA.magicalUses: 種植這種植物會産生保護作用。用於所有保護型和驅魔型的薰 香。將歐白芷撒在房子的四個角落,或是沿著房子周邊撒,可防止邪靈。加 到浴缸中，可以破除詛咒、咒語,和任何可能加諸在你身上的法術。
ANGELICA.lore: Nordic peoples called it the 'Root of the Holy Ghost'; legend says an angel revealed its plague-curing powers in a dream.

ANISE.magicalUses: 將大茴香的籽裝滿整個枕頭套,睡在上面,可確保不再做噩夢。 可製作用於保護和冥想的薰香。在房間放置新鮮的大茴香葉,可驅除邪恶， 有時也放在魔法陣周圍,保護法師免於惡靈的傷害。也可用來閃避邪眼。
ANISE.lore: Ancient Romans served anise-spiced cake at wedding feasts — the origin of the wedding cake tradition.

APPLE.ritualUses: 八月十三日是希臘的戴安娜音樂節(也就是羅馬神話中的維納 斯),在這一天，所準備的祭品中包含了還附在樹枝上的蘋果。
APPLE.magicalUses: 蘋果長久以來一直用於愛情咒語。將蘋果花放入愛情香包,熬煮 並調和薰香，讓它們融化在粉紅色的蠟中，然後風乾，就能製作出吸引愛情 的蠟燭。
APPLE.lore: The Celtic Otherworld Avalon means 'Isle of Apples'; cutting an apple crosswise reveals a pentagram of seeds.

APRICOT.magicalUses: 吃杏桃可獲得甜美的性格，另一種做法是在愛情咒語和「魔藥」 中加入其果汁。可將杏桃的葉子和花朵加到爱情香包中,攜帶其種子也可吸
APRICOT.lore: In Chinese folklore, apricots symbolize medicine and education; Confucius was said to have taught among apricot trees.

ARABIC,GUM.magicalUses: 添加到薰香中,可以達到良好的能量振動,或者將其個別放在木 炭上悶燒。可淨化負面能量和邪惡的領域。
ARABIC,GUM.lore: Traded along the Silk Road for millennia; ancient Egyptian scribes used it as binding agent for inks and pigments.

ARBUTUS.magicalUses: 羅馬人用它來驅逐邪恶，保護孩童。從古希臘時代開始，也用於 驅魔。
ARBUTUS.lore: The strawberry tree is the symbol of Madrid, Spain; its fruit was used in ancient Iberian fermented drinks.

ASAFOETIDA.magicalUses: 可在驅魔型和保護型的薰香中加入少量，也用於保護型的香 包，但會聞到奇怪的味道。在魔法儀式中，會将其扔到火上或是置於香爐 裡,可破壤靈的現身。
ASAFOETIDA.lore: Called 'Devil's Dung' for its pungent smell, yet prized in Indian cuisine and Persian medicine for thousands of years.

ASH.ritualUses: 對古代條頓人來説，歐洲樹代表「世界之樹」 (Y gdrasill), 這是他們對宇宙的概念，因此十分崇敬這種樹。
ASH.magicalUses: 將一塊歐洲梣樹的木材雕刻成一個太陽十字架(即四臂等長的方 形十字架)當作護身符,可在出海時預防溺水。這也用於祭海儀式,因為它 具有水的力量。
ASH.lore: In Norse mythology, Yggdrasil — the World Tree connecting all nine realms — is a great ash tree.

ASPEN.magicalUses: 用於防竊盜的法術,在花園或田裡種歐洲白楊木,可防小偷。
ASPEN.lore: Celtic druids believed aspens were trees of the dead; their perpetually trembling leaves symbolize communication with the spirit world.

ASTER.ritualUses: 翠菊對所有的神來説都是聖物，古希臘人在祭典期間會将其放在 寺廟的祭壇上。
ASTER.magicalUses: 用於愛情香包,攜帶盛開的花會赢得爱情。有人將其種在花園
ASTER.lore: In Greek myth, asters were created from the tears of the goddess Astraea as she wept over having too few stars on Earth.

AVENS.magicalUses: 用於驅魔型的薰香和混合藥草中,或是撒在要施法的區域周 圉。也用於淨化儀式。
AVENS.lore: Medieval monks grew avens in monastery gardens; its clove-scented root was believed to ward off evil spirits and venomous beasts.

AVOCADO.magicalUses: 古代的阿茲特克人咸信,吃酪梨的果實會充满慾望。不妨在家從 酪梨的種子開始種起,並將愛灌注進去。
AVOCADO.lore: The Aztecs called it 'ahuacatl' and considered it a fertility fruit; it was forbidden to virgins during harvest season.

BACHELOR'S.magicalUses: 女性將這種花佩戴在胸前,能吸引男人的愛。或者將一朵花放在
BACHELOR'S.lore: Named 'bachelor's buttons' because young men wore them to signal their romantic availability at country dances.

BALM,LEMON.magicalUses: 根據阿拉伯的魔藥學,檸檬香蜂草可用來影響愛情。将這種草浸 泡在葡萄酒中幾小時,瀝乾後與朋友分享,或隨身攜帶,能尋找愛情。
BALM,LEMON.lore: Paracelsus called it the 'Elixir of Life'; beekeepers have rubbed hives with lemon balm to attract swarms since ancient Greece.

BALM.ritualUses: 在中國的寺廟中會用竹子占卜。法師將竹片往祭拜者處丢去,根 據其落地的方式，來解讀是吉兆還是凶兆。
BALM.magicalUses: 攜帶基列香膏樹的枝枒,可修復 一
BALM.lore: Mentioned in the Bible as a precious healing resin from Gilead; the Queen of Sheba reportedly gifted it to King Solomon.

BANANA.ritualUses: 在夏威夷和大溪地向神靈獻祭時,有時會以香蕉柄代替人類祭 品。在夏威夷，直到一八一九年破除kapu ( 一種禁忌的密碼)前，某些種類 的香蕉是女性禁止食用的食物,偷吃者會被處死。當代巫毒教儀式中,會將 香蕉樹用來代表神靈,因為祂們和香蕉花一樣,都是雌雄同體的。
BANANA.magicalUses: 香蕉可用於增加生育熊力，也用於治療性無能。也許是因為這些 神奇的力量，所以如果新娘是在香蕉樹下結婚，好運就勢不可擋。
BANANA.lore: Hindu mythology considers the banana plant sacred to Vishnu and Lakshmi; in Hawaiian lore, bananas on fishing boats bring bad luck.

BANYAN.ritualUses: 印度教徒對孟加拉榕十分敬重,會將其種植在寺廟周圍。這種樹 在夏威夷和玻里尼希亞宗教中,都跟毛伊神的崇拜有關。
BANYAN.magicalUses: 光是坐在一棵孟加拉榕樹下，或是看著它，就能帶來好運。在樹 下舉行婚禮,可確保夫妻的幸福。
BANYAN.lore: In Hindu tradition, the banyan is the tree under which Shiva sits as the supreme yogi; its aerial roots symbolize immortality.

BARLEY.magicalUses: 在一些愛情法術中，會使用大麥的穀 粒及水來施行。
BARLEY.lore: One of the first domesticated grains, sacred to the Greek goddess Demeter; ancient Egyptians paid workers in bread and beer made from barley.

BASIL.lore: Sacred to Vishnu and Krishna in Hinduism; in Greek, 'basilikon' means 'royal herb,' and it was used in coronation rituals.
BASIL.magicalUses: Basil is used in love spells and sachets. It brings wealth when carried in the pocket or placed in cash registers. Sprinkled on the floor of a business, it attracts customers. Also used in purification baths and exorcism incenses.

BAY.ritualUses: 古代阿波羅的女祭司會咀嚼月桂葉以進入預言状態,還會吸其煙 霧。在古日耳曼民族的宗教節日耶魯節 ( Yule), 也就是日後接受基督教化 而更名的聖誕節,會用月桂葉來作装飾品。
BAY.magicalUses: 在熬煮預言和智慧型藥草時會使用月桂葉,儘管它的味道很 濃。将月桂葉放在枕頭下，會誘發預言夢境，燃燒它也會來引發幻覺。
BAY.lore: The Oracle at Delphi chewed bay leaves before prophesying; victorious Roman generals wore laurel wreaths — the origin of 'laureate.'

BEAN.ritualUses: 有些菜豆的花是白色的，對收穫女神而言是神聖的，因此是獻給 古老女神的聖物。在蘇格蘭,根據傳統只有最高層級的女祭司可以種植或烹 煮菜豆。古羅馬在六月一日,會將菜豆連同豬肉一起獻給女神卡爾迪亞。
BEAN.magicalUses: 一般來説，在古典時期(現在仍然)會用菜豆來抵抗邪恶巫師的 迷術。把菜豆含在嘴神，然後朝施法者吐去。
BEAN.lore: Ancient Romans threw beans at ghosts during the festival of Lemuria; Pythagoras forbade his followers from eating them.

BEDSTRAW,FRAGRANT.magicalUses: 佩戴或攜帶蓬子菜可吸引愛情。
BEDSTRAW,FRAGRANT.lore: Legend says the Virgin Mary's manger was filled with bedstraw, which bloomed golden on Christmas night.

BEECH.magicalUses: 拿一根歐洲山毛櫸的枝條,將願望畫或刻在其上,把它埋進土地 裡,然後留在那裡。若命中注定,你的願望將會成真。
BEECH.lore: Anglo-Saxon runes were first carved on beech wood tablets; the English word 'book' derives from the Old English for beech.

BEET.magicalUses: 若是一對男女吃了同一顆甜菜,他們會墜入愛河。 甜菜汁可用作愛情魔法中的墨水，也可代替血液。
BEET.lore: Ancient Greeks offered beets to Apollo at his temple in Delphi; Roman lovers used beet juice as an aphrodisiac.

BELLADONNA.ritualUses: 根據古老的傳統,女戰神貝羅纳的祭司在進行祭拜前，要先喝一 口顛茄汁。
BELLADONNA.magicalUses: 在今日，由於顛茄的高毒性，鲜少用於藥草魔法，整株植物都含 有劇毒，到現在仍然有人因誤食而死的意外發生。
BELLADONNA.lore: Renaissance Italian women dropped belladonna extract into their eyes to dilate pupils for beauty — hence 'beautiful lady.'

BENZOIN.magicalUses: 可燃燒安息香來淨化；或加到淨化型薰香中。這是一種很好的 「清潔」藥草。
BENZOIN.lore: Used as temple incense across Southeast Asia for centuries; Arab traders called it 'luban jawi' — frankincense of Java.

BERGAMOT,ORANGE.magicalUses: 将檸檬薄荷的葉子插在皮夾和錢包
BERGAMOT,ORANGE.lore: The distinctive flavor of Earl Grey tea; named after the Italian city of Bergamo where the oil was first traded.

BERGAMOT,WILD.magicalUses: 蜂香薄荷可用來釐清各種情况的表象,帶來工作秩序。
BERGAMOT,WILD.lore: Native Americans brewed 'Oswego tea' from wild bergamot long before European contact; it was a Boston Tea Party substitute.

BETONY,WOOD.magicalUses: 藥水蘇一直是用於保護和淨化的藥草。偽託古羅馬學者阿普列尤 斯的中世紀藥草書上，記載這種植物可以保護佩戴者的靈魂和身體,将其放 在枕頭下方，可以防止看見異象和作噩夢。
BETONY,WOOD.lore: Roman physician Antonius Musa wrote an entire treatise claiming betony cured 47 different ailments.

BIRCH.magicalUses: 由於樺樹是一種淨化或清潔的藥草,所以會拿樺樹的枝條輕輕拍 打遭到附身的人或動物，藉以驅除邪靈。
BIRCH.lore: The first tree to recolonize after the Ice Age, earning it the first letter (Beth) in the Celtic Ogham tree alphabet.

BISTORT.magicalUses: 若是想懷孕,就隨身攜帶拳參。與乳香一起燃燒,可提升靈 力,或是在占卜時使用。
BISTORT.lore: Its twisted root earned the name 'twice-twisted'; English pudding-dock was traditionally eaten at Easter in Northern England.

BITTERSWEET.magicalUses: 在枕頭下方放一些南蛇藤有助於忘記過去的愛。
BITTERSWEET.lore: Also called 'woody nightshade'; medieval physicians hung it around patients' necks to ward off the evil eye.

BLACKBERRY.ritualUses: 過去黑莓對歐洲一些古老的異教神靈來説是神聖的，並用於這些 神靈的崇拜。
BLACKBERRY.magicalUses: 形成自然拱形的黑莓荆棘，在治療魔法中有很大的用處。陽光明 媚的日子,在黑莓拱門下爬行三次,盡可能由東向西。這可治療癤、風濕 病、百日咳，甚至是黑頭粉刺。
BLACKBERRY.lore: Celtic lore says blackberries become cursed after Michaelmas (Sept 29) when the devil spits on them.

BLADDERWRACK.magicalUses: 墨角藻通常可以保護在海上的人， 或飛越海洋上空的人。因此,洲際旅行者應隨身攜帶。它也用在海術上,將 其扔到海浪上，並召喚海精靈,可獲得他們的青睐，幫助魔法的施展。
BLADDERWRACK.lore: Victorian-era women used this seaweed in beauty baths; it was the original source of iodine, discovered in 1811.

BLEEDING.magicalUses: 將花朵捏碎,若花汁是紅色的,那麼你的愛人就有一顆對你充满 愛意的心；若是白的，他或她就不愛你。
BLEEDING.lore: In Japanese legend, each part of the flower tells a tragic love story; the plant symbolizes unconditional love.

BLOODROOT.magicalUses: 攜帶或佩帶血根草可吸引愛情,也可以用來避免邪惡咒語和負面 力量。
BLOODROOT.lore: Native Americans used its vivid red sap as war paint and ceremonial dye; the Algonquin used it as a love charm.

BLUEBELL.magicalUses: 若是能將一朵圓葉風鈴草花由內而
BLUEBELL.lore: British folklore warns that fairies hang their spells on bluebells; picking one invites fairy mischief.

BLUEBERRY.magicalUses: 放一些藍莓在腳踏墊下方，可驅離 那些不受歡迎者遠離你的家門。
BLUEBERRY.lore: Native Americans called blueberries 'star berries' because of the five-pointed star shape at the blossom end.

BLUE.magicalUses: 攜帶其根部,可獲取經濟利益。也可將藍旗鳶尾根放在收銀機
BLUE.lore: Sacred to Native American healers; used in purification ceremonies and as protection against serpents.

BODHI.ritualUses: 這種植物是祭拜毗濕奴的聖物，就跟佛陀在菩提樹下開悟一 様，據説毗濕奴是出生在這種樹下。
BODHI.magicalUses: 若是在附近感到有邪惡,只需要繞這棵樹幾圈,邪靈就會害怕地 逃離。
BODHI.lore: Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment while meditating under a Bodhi tree; the original tree in Bodh Gaya is still venerated.

BONESET.magicalUses: 這種植物可以防止邪靈。
BONESET.lore: Named because it was used to treat 'break-bone fever' (dengue); Native Americans considered it one of their most important medicines.

BORAGE.magicalUses: 攜帶新鮮的琉璃苣花可以增加勇氣。在戶外行走時,將一朵花插 放在衣服鈕卸洞中，可以産生保護作用。
BORAGE.lore: Roman soldiers drank borage wine for courage before battle; the old saying goes, 'I, Borage, bring always courage.'

BRACKEN.magicalUses: 若在户外燃燒歐洲蕨，就會下雨。
BRACKEN.lore: Cutting a bracken fern root crosswise reveals the initials 'JC' or an oak tree pattern in Celtic tradition.

BRAZILNUT.magicalUses: 將其當作護身符攜帶,會在感情方面帶來好運。
BRAZILNUT.lore: Each nut pod weighs up to 5 pounds and falls from 160-foot trees; Amazonian peoples have harvested them for 11,000+ years.

BRIONY.magicalUses: 瀉根通常用在各種幻術的操作中，並代替罕見的曼德拉草根。
BRIONY.lore: In medieval Europe, briony root was carved into 'mandrake' shape and sold as the more expensive magical root.

BROMELIAD.magicalUses: 在家中種植小鳳梨，可帶來金錢和奢侈品。其植株本身也有保護 作用，可説是室内植物的良好選擇。
BROMELIAD.lore: The pineapple, most famous bromeliad, was a symbol of hospitality in colonial America, displayed on gateposts and furniture.

BROOM.magicalUses: 金雀花用於淨化和保護法術,掛在家中可防止邪惡。此外,在屋 內噴灑其浸劑,也能驅離搗蛋作亂者。
BROOM.lore: Witches were said to ride broom plants (Planta genista); the plant gave its name to the Plantagenet royal dynasty of England.

BUCHU.magicalUses: 醉酒時喝下南非香葉木浸劑,就能看見未來。
BUCHU.lore: Used by the indigenous Khoisan people of South Africa for over a thousand years as both medicine and a body-cleansing fragrance.

BUCKTHORN.magicalUses: 古羅馬《藥物論》作者迪奧斯克理德斯( Dioscorides) 表示,將 歐鼠李的樹枝放在門邊與窗邊,可驅離魔咒和巫師。
BUCKTHORN.lore: Ethiopian legend says buckthorn was the wood used for Christ's crown of thorns; it has been used as a magical barrier since antiquity.

BUCKWHEAT.magicalUses: 研磨種子(製成麥粉)撒在房子周圍,可防止邪靈。或是在施行 魔法時,在周圍的地板上撒上蕎麥粉,可形成一魔法結界。
BUCKWHEAT.lore: Despite its name, buckwheat is not wheat at all; Japanese monks brought it to make soba noodles, which became a New Year's tradition.

BURDOCK.magicalUses: 擺放在居家環境周圍,可抵禦負面力量。可添加到保護型薰香 中，或是用於這類法術。
BURDOCK.lore: In 1941, a Swiss engineer noticed burdock burrs clinging to his dog's fur, inspiring the invention of Velcro.

CABBAGE.magicalUses: 如果希望在婚姻生活中擁有好運,新婚夫婦婚後的第一件事，就 是在花園中種植甘藍,這也能為花園帶來好運。
CABBAGE.lore: Ancient Egyptians and Romans ate cabbage before banquets believing it prevented drunkenness — an early 'hangover prevention.'

CACTUS.magicalUses: 由於带刺，所有種類的仙人掌都具 有保護作用。
CACTUS.lore: The Aztec capital Tenochtitlan was founded where an eagle perched on a cactus eating a snake — now Mexico's coat of arms.

CALAMUS.magicalUses: 将其種子做成串珠,可用於治療,或是將根磨成粉末,加在治療 類型的薰香和香包中。
CALAMUS.lore: Listed in Exodus as an ingredient of the holy anointing oil; Vedic texts call it 'vacha' and link it to eloquent speech.

CAMELLIA.magicalUses: 山茶花能带來財富和奢侈品，因此會用於這類的法術中。在祈求
CAMELLIA.lore: In the Japanese language of flowers (Hanakotoba), the camellia symbolizes a noble death; samurai admired how its blossoms fall whole.

CAMPHOR.magicalUses: 聞到會減少性慾,放在床邊也有同樣的效果。但是,將一包樟腦 (或樟樹的樹皮)掛在脖子上，可以防止感冒和流感。
CAMPHOR.lore: Arab traders brought camphor from Borneo to the Mediterranean; it was worth its weight in gold in medieval Europe.

CAPER.magicalUses: 有陽痿問題的男性,只要吃一些續隨子就能獲得治癒。
CAPER.lore: Ancient Greeks and Romans used capers as both medicine and aphrodisiac; they appear in the Epic of Gilgamesh.

CARAWAY.magicalUses: 葛縷子有保護作用，可對抗法力高強的莉莉絲 (Lilith, 是蘇美 爾神話與猶太教拉比文學中的夜之魔女,被指為亞當的第一位妻子),以及 各種邪靈、邪物和一般古老的負面力量，這是通常的用途。
CARAWAY.lore: Ancient superstition held that caraway prevents theft — placing seeds in any object would keep it from being stolen.

CARDAMON.magicalUses: 将研磨過的小豆蔻種子加到溫熱的酒水中,就能夠迅速得到一憋 望魔藥。
CARDAMON.lore: Called the 'Queen of Spices' in India; ancient Egyptians chewed cardamom pods to clean their teeth and freshen breath.

CARNATION.magicalUses: 在伊莉莎白時代會戴上康乃馨，防止在鷹架上死亡；康乃馨可用 於通用的保護型法術。
CARNATION.lore: In Korean tradition, red carnations honor living parents while white ones honor the deceased — the origin of Mother's Day flowers.

CAROB.magicalUses: 隨身擼帶可維持健康,對抗邪惡。
CAROB.lore: Also called 'locust bean,' tradition says John the Baptist survived on carobs in the wilderness; the word 'carat' derives from carob seeds.

CARROT.lore: Medieval Europeans believed carrots helped one see in the dark — a belief the British military revived as WWII propaganda to conceal radar.

CASCARA.magicalUses: 在上法院進行任何訴訟前，噴灑美鼠李浸劑在住家附近，有助於
CASCARA.lore: Spanish missionaries named it 'sacred bark'; Pacific Northwest peoples had used it medicinally for centuries before.

CASHEW.magicalUses: 腰果多用於發達和金錢的法術中。
CASHEW.lore: The cashew 'nut' actually grows outside the fruit; Portuguese colonizers spread it from Brazil to India and Africa in the 1500s.

CASTOR.magicalUses: 蓖麻的豆子具有良好的保護作用，可對抗邪眼以及所有負面力
CASTOR.lore: Castor oil was called 'palma Christi' (hand of Christ) in medieval Europe; ancient Egyptians burned it in lamps 4,000 years ago.

CATNIP.magicalUses: 給你的貓一點貓薄荷,會在你們之間創造出一種心靈聯繫。它也 會讓貓陶醉。
CATNIP.lore: Roman herbalist Pliny wrote about catnip's effects on cats; legend says that hangmen drank catnip tea for courage.

CAT.magicalUses: 如果一個女人無法享受魚水之歡,但希望能夠改善,便應該隨身 攜带一些香蒲。
CAT.lore: Indigenous peoples across North America used every part of the cattail — a true survival plant for food, shelter, and medicine.

CEDAR.magicalUses: 雪松的煙霧有淨化作用,還能改善噩夢的問題,可將雪松的枝條 燒成碳、悶燒或製成香來應用。美洲印第安人在治療頭部感冒時,會將雪松 放在三温暖的熱石上來淨化。
CEDAR.lore: The ancient Sumerians built the world's first epic poem around a cedar forest; Solomon's Temple was built with Lebanon's sacred cedars.

CELANDINE.magicalUses: 白屈菜有助於逃避無端遭到的監禁和誘捕。将其穿戴在身上，與 皮膚直接接觸,每三天更换一次，便可達到這種效果。
CELANDINE.lore: Its name comes from Greek 'chelidon' (swallow); ancients believed the flower bloomed when swallows arrived and faded when they left.

CELERY.magicalUses: 咀嚼芹菜籽有助於集中注意力，或是用於施術的枕頭,可誘導
CELERY.lore: Ancient Greek athletes wore celery wreaths; the word 'celery' comes from the Greek word for parsley — they considered them related.

CENTAURY.lore: Named for the centaur Chiron, who in Greek myth used this herb to heal a wound from Hercules' poisoned arrow.
CENTAURY.magicalUses: Used to repel snakes and drive away anger. Added to incenses for their purifying effects.

CHAMOMILE,GERMAN.magicalUses: 燃燒百金花的煙霧可驅蛇。
CHAMOMILE,GERMAN.lore: Ancient Egyptians dedicated chamomile to their sun god Ra; the Anglo-Saxons listed it as one of the Nine Sacred Herbs.

CHERRY.magicalUses: 長久以來,樱桃就用於刺激或吸引愛情。有個美麗的日本愛情魔 法,相當簡單,只要將一根頭髮綁在盛開的櫻花樹上即可。
CHERRY.lore: Japanese Hanami (cherry blossom viewing) has been celebrated for over a thousand years; the fleeting blooms symbolize the beauty of impermanence.

CHESTNUT.magicalUses: 在愛情魔法中會使用栗子,或直接將其給所愛之人食用。
CHESTNUT.lore: In many European traditions, carrying a chestnut in your pocket prevents backaches and rheumatism.

CHICKWEED.lore: Called 'stellaria' for its tiny star-shaped flowers; birds love it so much that its common name refers to feeding chickens.
CHICKWEED.magicalUses: Carried to attract love or maintain a relationship. Also used in spells for fertility and fidelity.

CHICORY.magicalUses: 隨身带或用於法術,可吸引愛情，或保持關係。
CHICORY.lore: German folklore says chicory is an enchanted maiden waiting by the road for her lover, turned into a flower by the gods.

CHILI.magicalUses: 若是覺得你的伴侶正在騎驢找馬,買兩條大的乾辣椒，以一條紅
CHILI.lore: Cultivated in the Americas for over 7,500 years; the Aztecs used chili smoke as a form of chemical warfare.

CHINA.magicalUses: 苦楝的種子多應用於招來好運的魔法，带在身上也能改變生活 品質。
CHINA.lore: This herb may refer to Smilax china, used in traditional Chinese medicine for centuries to treat various ailments.

CHRYSANTHEMUM.magicalUses: 喝一杯菊花茶，可舒緩醉酒。
CHRYSANTHEMUM.lore: The Japanese Imperial throne is called the 'Chrysanthemum Throne'; the flower symbolizes longevity and rejuvenation in East Asian culture.

CINCHONA.magicalUses: 隨身攜帶一塊金雞納樹皮可帶來好 運 ,並且可保護身體不受到傷害和邪靈騷擾。
CINCHONA.lore: Source of quinine, the first effective malaria treatment; Spanish Jesuits learned of it from Quechua healers in Peru.

CINNAMON.ritualUses: 古希伯來人将肉桂油作為神聖膏油的一部分。古羅馬的神廟 中,裝飾有肉桂樹葉子編織成的花圈。埃及人在製作木乃伊的過程中,也會 使用肉桂油。
CINNAMON.magicalUses: 将肉桂當作薰香燃燒時,會引起高度的精神振動,有助於治 療、招財並産生保護性振動。
CINNAMON.lore: Ancient spice traders fabricated stories of giant birds guarding cinnamon to keep its source secret and prices high.

CINQUEFOIL.magicalUses: 葉子上的五個點分別代表愛情、金錢、健康、力量和智慧,所以 擴帶委陵菜就能確保這些特質。
CINQUEFOIL.lore: Medieval witches reputedly used cinquefoil in flying ointments; its five-lobed leaf was associated with the five senses.

CITRON.lore: One of the original citrus fruits; the Jewish festival of Sukkot requires a perfect citron (etrog) as a ceremonial object.

CLEAVERS.lore: Also called 'goosegrass' because geese love it; its tiny hooks inspired early textile carding tools.
CLEAVERS.magicalUses: Used in commitment and binding spells. The plant's clinging nature makes it useful in love sachets.

CLOTH-OF-GOLD.magicalUses: 猪殃殃會攀附在織物上，這可以用於強化法術。
CLOTH-OF-GOLD.lore: This crocus relative's golden stamens produce saffron, the world's most expensive spice — worth more than gold by weight.

CLOVE.magicalUses: 當成薰香燃燒,可吸引財富、驅除敵意和負面力量,產生精神振 動 ,淨化該區域，也可阻止别人對你的間言間語。
CLOVE.lore: Chinese courtiers in the Han Dynasty were required to hold cloves in their mouths when addressing the emperor, to sweeten their breath.

CLOVER.magicalUses: 雙葉:如果你能找到一片雙葉的三葉草，很快就會找到愛情。
CLOVER.lore: The Druids considered four-leaf clovers magical charms; St. Patrick used the three-leaf clover to explain the Holy Trinity.

CLUB.magicalUses: 以正確方法採集，這種藥草會带來神的保護、力量和祝福。在流 水中沐浴淨身，獻上麵包和葡萄酒，然後用小指或銀刀将其連根拔起，它就 會具有強大的威力。
CLUB.lore: Club moss spores are so fine and flammable they were used as flash powder in Victorian stage magic and early photography.

COHOSH.magicalUses: 在愛情香包中使用黑升麻，並在浴缸中加入其浸劑,有助於陽痿 的治療。
COHOSH.lore: Cherokee and Iroquois women used black cohosh for centuries; its name in Algonquin means 'rough and knotty root.'

COLTSFOOT.magicalUses: 可添加在愛情香包中；用於尋求和平與安寧的法術。吸入其葉子 的煙霧,會引起幻覺。
COLTSFOOT.lore: One of the earliest spring flowers, once used as an apothecary symbol; its Latin name 'Tussilago' means 'cough dispeller.'

COLUMBINE.magicalUses: 以此藥草摩擦手，可激發勇氣,變得大膽,或可隨身带。
COLUMBINE.lore: In medieval art, columbine symbolized the Holy Spirit; its name comes from 'columba' (dove) — the petals resemble a circle of doves.

COMFREY.magicalUses: 穿戴或隨身攜帶,可產生保護作用,並確保旅行期間的安全。另 外,也可放一些在行李箱內,可避免遺失或被偷。
COMFREY.lore: Called 'knitbone' since Roman times for its legendary ability to mend broken bones; medieval travelers carried it for safe journeys.

COPAL.magicalUses: 柯巴樹會添加到愛情和淨化薰香中，特别是在墨西哥。
COPAL.lore: The Aztecs burned copal as incense to feed the gods; the word comes from Nahuatl 'copalli' meaning 'incense.'

CORIANDER.magicalUses: 長久以來,芫荽一直用於爱情的香包和法術中。将粉狀種子加到 溫熱的酒中,可製成慾望魔藥。
CORIANDER.lore: One of the oldest known spices, found in Tutankhamun's tomb; referenced in the Book of Exodus as resembling manna.

CORN.ritualUses: 玉米之母，或是玉米女神，是主管豐收和生育的神祇，在整個北 美洲東部長期受到崇拜。美國新墨西哥州的祖尼人( Zunis) 在他們的宗教 儀式中，常會使用不同顔色的玉米。藍玉米粉用來祝福，會灑在大地上作為 祭品。
CORN.magicalUses: 拿一根玉米,随意拉出玉米穗,計算上面的玉米粒。每十二粒玉 米代表一年,由此可得知你的年龄。将玉米穗放在搖籃內,可保護寶寶免受 負面力量的影響。
CORN.lore: Sacred to countless Native American peoples, corn is one of the 'Three Sisters' planted together with squash and beans.

COTTON.magicalUses: 如果將一塊棉花放入糖碗中,就會有好運降臨;在黎明時將棉花 丢過右肩,也會有同樣的效果。在後者這種情況下,好運將會在白天結束前 到來。
COTTON.lore: Ancient Indus Valley civilizations wove cotton 5,000 years ago; Greek historian Herodotus described it as 'tree wool.'

COWSLIP.magicalUses: 如果不想被人打擾,在前廊下方放一點黃花九輪草,可以阻止訪 客上門。
COWSLIP.lore: In English folklore, cowslips mark the entrance to fairy realms; Shakespeare mentions them as fairy favorites in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

CROCUS.magicalUses: 這種植物長大後會吸引愛情。
CROCUS.lore: In Greek myth, the youth Crocus was turned into this flower; autumn crocuses yield saffron, the world's most precious spice.

CUBEB.magicalUses: 以草澄茄的漿果應用於愛情香包和法術中。
CUBEB.lore: Medieval European spice merchants imported cubeb pepper from Java; it was once more popular than black pepper in Western cuisine.

CUCKOO-FLOWER.magicalUses: 草甸碎米薺的新鮮塊莖可用於爱情魔法;佩戴在身上,可增加受 孕機會,若佩戴大塊莖將會產下男嬰,若是小的,则是女嬰。
CUCKOO-FLOWER.lore: Blooms in spring when the cuckoo starts singing; picking it was said to invite thunderstorms in English folklore.

CUCUMBER.magicalUses: 吃黃瓜的果實會降低慾望。
CUCUMBER.lore: Ancient Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans all cultivated cucumbers; Emperor Tiberius demanded them at his table every day of the year.

CUMIN.magicalUses: 在德國和義大利,會將孜然放入麵包中,以防止木靈偷麵包。孜 然種子擁有「保留的特性」,可防止任何含有它的物體遭到偷竊。
CUMIN.lore: In medieval Europe, cumin symbolized fidelity — brides and grooms carried it during weddings to ensure faithfulness.

CURRY.magicalUses: 在黃昏時燃燒咖哩葉(是一種特定的植物,而不是用於烹飪的香 料混合物),可防止邪惡力量的影響。
CURRY.lore: The curry leaf tree is sacred in Hindu tradition; ancient Tamil texts describe its culinary and medicinal uses over 2,000 years ago.

CYCLAMEN.magicalUses: 在卧室中擺一盆仙客來,可保護在房中睡眠的人；據説在有種植 仙客來的地方，所有有害的法術都無法起作用。
CYCLAMEN.lore: Also called 'sowbread' because wild pigs dig up its tubers; ancient physicians associated it with the womb and fertility.

CYPRESS.ritualUses: 古代的米諾斯人崇拜絲柏,將其當作是神聖的象徵,並將這種信 仰從克里特島傳到塞浦路斯。在埃及,會使用絲柏的木材來製作棺材。
CYPRESS.magicalUses: 在面臨危機時可使用絲柏,特别是在朋友或親戚去世時。在葬禮 佩戴或攜帶,可以緩解心靈,減輕悲痛。
CYPRESS.lore: The ancient Greeks planted cypresses in cemeteries; the tree's name may derive from the island of Cyprus, sacred to Aphrodite.

DAFFODIL.magicalUses: 在施作愛情法術時,會將水仙花放在祭壇上,随身攜帶亦可達到
DAFFODIL.lore: In Greek myth, Narcissus was turned into this flower after falling in love with his own reflection.

DAISY.magicalUses: 據說摘下當季第一朵雛菊的人,將擁有無法控制的「撒嬌心 態」。睡覺時將雛菊的根放在枕頭下面,離開的爱人有可能會回到你身 邊。佩戴在身上，雛菊會帶來愛情。
DAISY.lore: The English name comes from 'day's eye' — the flower opens at dawn and closes at dusk, following the sun.

DAMIANA.magicalUses: 多用於製作煞望的浸劑以及法術。燃 燒它也會産生幻覺。
DAMIANA.lore: Used as an aphrodisiac by the Maya and Aztec civilizations; Mexican tradition says the first margarita was made with damiana liqueur.

DANDELION.magicalUses: 要知道夀命有多長,你會活多久?朝著蒲公英的頭吹一口氣,剩 下的種子即代表你還剩下的年數。
DANDELION.lore: Its name comes from French 'dent de lion' (lion's tooth); every part of the plant is edible and has been used in folk medicine worldwide.

DATURA.ritualUses: 不知有多少個世紀,蕯滿教徒一直有使用曼陀羅,並且用在宗教 儀式中。阿茲特克人認為這種植物是神聖的。
DATURA.magicalUses: 曼陀羅可用來破除咒語,只要撒在房子四周即可。它還可用來防 止邪靈。若是連續失眠好幾晚，可以在每只鞋子中放一些曼陀羅的葉子，然 後將鞋子放在床下,腳趾的方向朝最近的牆壁,便能解决失眠問題。
DATURA.lore: Sacred to Shiva in Hindu tradition; Native American peoples used it in vision quests, though it is extremely dangerous.

DEERSTONGUE.magicalUses: 穿戴或攜帶在身,可吸引男性。將鹿舌草撒在床上,也有同樣的
DEERSTONGUE.lore: Appalachian folk magic uses deerstongue for eloquence; its leaves contain coumarin, giving them a vanilla-like scent.

DEVIL'S.magicalUses: 将山蘿蔔戴在脖子上，會驅走邪 靈 ,提供保護。
DEVIL'S.lore: Various plants share this ominous name; 'devil's bit' was said to have had its root bitten off by the devil out of spite.

DILL.magicalUses: 將這種藥草做成的保護型香包掛在門上或隨身攜帶,具有保護作 用。放在搖籃裡可以保護孩子。如果把它放在門上,心懷惡意或嫉妒你的人 就無法進入你家。
DILL.lore: Norse warriors drank dill water for courage; the name comes from Old Norse 'dilla' meaning 'to soothe.'

DITTANY.magicalUses: 燃燒的白藓是絕佳的顯靈劑基底； 靈會出現在香爐升起的煙霧中。
DITTANY.lore: Ancient Greeks believed wild goats on Crete ate this herb to heal arrow wounds; it was one of the rarest magical herbs.

DOCK.magicalUses: 大羊蹄的種子可用於財富型法術和
DOCK.lore: A universal folk remedy — 'dock leaf for nettle sting' is one of the oldest pieces of herbal knowledge in European tradition.

DODDER.magicalUses: 用於占卜愛情時,摘下菟絲子,将其丢過所寄生的植物(菟絲子 是寄生生物),然後隔天返回這株植物，如果菟絲子再次附著在植物上，那 就表示你的意中人爱你,如果没有,就表示他不爱你。
DODDER.lore: This parasitic vine has no chlorophyll and survives by draining host plants — earning it the folk name 'devil's guts.'

DOGBANE.lore: Native Americans twisted its tough fibers into cordage, fishing nets, and fabric; early colonists used it similarly.
DOGBANE.magicalUses: Used in love magic; the flowers are added to sachets and mixtures for love and attraction.

DOGWOOD.magicalUses: 可以應用在愛情魔藥的混合物中。
DOGWOOD.lore: Christian legend says the dogwood was once a tall tree used for the cross, then cursed to remain small and twisted forever.

DRAGON'S.magicalUses: 燃燒這種棕櫚樹的樹脂,可讓犯錯的愛人返回身邊。通常是由女 性在夜晚時坐在開著的窗户旁來施行。
DRAGON'S.lore: The bright red resin has been traded since antiquity; Romans used it as dye, and Stradivari may have used it on his violins.

DULSE.magicalUses: 加在飲品中會料誘導慾望產生,灑在家裡會促進和諧。
DULSE.lore: Irish monks sustained themselves on dulse seaweed during long fasts; it has been a coastal food in the British Isles for over a thousand years.

DUTCHMAN'S.magicalUses: 将兜狀荷包牡丹的根佩戴在身上，可 吸引愛情。
DUTCHMAN'S.lore: The pipe-shaped flower inspired its name; Native Americans used the root as a snakebite remedy.

EBONY.magicalUses: 豆柿具有保護作用，因此會用來製 作護身符。
EBONY.lore: Ancient Egyptian pharaohs prized ebony wood; it was among the tribute items depicted in Queen Hatshepsut's temple.

ECHINACEA.magicalUses: 美洲印第安人會用狹葉紫錐花作為獻給靈的祭品,從而確保和加
ECHINACEA.lore: Plains Indians used echinacea more than any other herb; Cheyenne warriors chewed the root to numb pain before battle.

EDELWEISS.magicalUses: 将高山火絨草做成花圈穿戴在身 上，可隱形。
EDELWEISS.lore: Alpine symbol of courage — suitors risked their lives climbing to pick it; the Sound of Music made it world famous.

ELDER,AMERICAN.ritualUses: 在古代英國的墓室中，會應用這種接骨木於墓葬儀式中。由於花 朵是白色，是祭拜許多女神的聖物。
ELDER,AMERICAN.magicalUses: 若是將接骨木穿戴在身上,可以抵禦各種攻擊者。掛在門口和窗 戶上,能夠驅除邪惡。
ELDER,AMERICAN.lore: Native Americans made flutes and arrows from elder; the Elder Mother mythology crossed the Atlantic with colonists.

ELECAMPANE.magicalUses: 将土木香穿戴在身上，會吸引愛情。
ELECAMPANE.lore: Legend says Helen of Troy carried elecampane when Paris abducted her; its Latin name 'Inula' may derive from Helen.

ELM.magicalUses: 由於榆樹在精靈中相當受歡迎， 一度被稱為「精靈樹」 (Elv en )
ELM.lore: In Norse mythology, the first woman (Embla) was created from an elm tree, while the first man came from an ash.

ENDIVE.magicalUses: 用於魔法時,最好是依下列方式採集：在六月二十七日或七月
ENDIVE.lore: Ancient Egyptians cultivated endive; the Blue Chicory Fairy in Cicely Mary Barker's Flower Fairies represents its wild relative.

ERYNGO.magicalUses: 旅行者擴帶或穿戴刺芹,可以確保旅途中的安全和運氣。 這種藥草也可带來和平，可撒在某個地方，或是給予爭吵中的夫婦。 吃下刺芹會引發慾望,所以這也用於所有類型的愛情咒語。
ERYNGO.lore: Elizabethan England considered candied eryngo root a powerful aphrodisiac; Shakespeare references it in The Merry Wives of Windsor.

EUCALYPTUS.magicalUses: 會用藍桉葉子來填充治療型的人偶,隨身攜帶,可保持良好的健 康狀態。要舒緩感冒,將葉子和豆莢環繞綠色蠟燭,在容器內燃燒,並在腦 中想像病患(或是自己)完全健康的景象。
EUCALYPTUS.lore: Australia's iconic tree; Aboriginal peoples used eucalyptus medicinally for over 40,000 years before European colonization.

EUPHORBIA.magicalUses: 在安曼，婦人分娩後,會拿一枝飛揚草進屋，用以潔淨。
EUPHORBIA.lore: Named after King Juba II's personal physician Euphorbus; the genus contains over 2,000 species on every continent.

EYEBRIGHT.magicalUses: 將小米草釀成茶飲用,可提神醒腦、提升記憶。
EYEBRIGHT.lore: The Doctrine of Signatures said its flower resembled an eye, so it must cure eye ailments — and people have used it for exactly that since the 14th century.

FENNEL.ritualUses: 在祭拜酒神的儀式中，經常會用大的茴香莖來製作酒神權杖，其 末端還附上松果。
FENNEL.magicalUses: 在家附近種植茴香，可産生保護作用。
FENNEL.lore: Greek warriors ate fennel before battle at Marathon; the Greek word for fennel, 'marathon,' gave the famous battle its name.

FENUGREEK.magicalUses: 要讓家裡錢財滾滾,可以在拖地水中加入一些胡蘆巴種子(或是 倒入少量的胡蘆巴浸劑)。另外,也可放一個裝入半瓶胡蘆巴的小罐子在 房子裡,並將瓶蓋打開,亦可招財。每隔幾天加幾粒種子,直到將罐子裝 滿
FENUGREEK.lore: Ancient Egyptians used fenugreek in embalming; it appears in one of the oldest known medical texts, the Ebers Papyrus (1550 BCE).

FERN.magicalUses: 蕨類具有保護作用，因此會插在花瓶中，也會将其種在門口。放 在室内，也具有保護作用。
FERN.lore: Slavic folklore says fern flowers bloom only at midnight on Ivan Kupala Night, and finding one grants wishes and reveals treasure.

FEVERFEW.lore: Its name comes from Latin 'febrifuga' (fever reducer); medieval Europeans planted it around houses to purify the air.
FEVERFEW.magicalUses: Carried for protection against accidents and illness during travel. Planted around the house for purification.

FIG.magicalUses: 隨身攜带有保護作用,能抵禦感冒、發燒以及意外事故。
FIG.lore: The Buddha attained enlightenment under a fig (Bodhi) tree; ancient Olympians ate figs for strength and wore fig wreaths as crowns.

FIGWORT.magicalUses: 掛在脖子上，玄参可維持健康，並抵禦邪眼。也可以在盛夏時間 以火燃燒這種植物，然後掛在家中，可産生保護的力量。
FIGWORT.lore: Named for its knobby roots resembling the swellings of scrofula (fig-like sores), the disease it was believed to cure.

FLAX.ritualUses: 亞麻用於祭拜條頓女神胡爾達的儀式中,因為是衪首先教導凡人 種植亞麻,並將其紡成亞麻線,編織成布。
FLAX.magicalUses: 亞麻籽可用於金錢法術。放一些在口袋、錢包或皮夾中，或是放 一個罐子在祭壇上，加上一些錢幣,再放入一些亞麻籽。每天重複上述做 法,可以招財。在鞋子裡放一點亞麻可以防止貧困。
FLAX.lore: Ancient Egyptians wrapped mummies in linen made from flax; the plant has been cultivated for over 10,000 years.

FLEABANE.magicalUses: 自古以來就有使用蚤草來驅除邪靈,防止進入家中。要做到這一
FLEABANE.lore: Named because burning it was believed to drive away fleas; Roman naturalist Pliny documented this use.

FOXGLOVE.magicalUses: 種在花園裡,可保護花園和家庭。過去英國威爾斯地區的家庭主 婦會用毛地黃的葉子製作黑色染料,在他們小屋的石頭地板上畫出交叉線 條,藉以防止邪恶入侵。
FOXGLOVE.lore: The source of the heart drug digitalis; folk names like 'fairy gloves' and 'witches' thimbles' connect it to the fairy realm.

FRANKINCENSE.ritualUses: 古埃及人在日出時會燃燒燒乳香，膜拜古埃及太陽神拉。時至今 日，乳香卻成了天主教堂所使用的一些薰香成分。
FRANKINCENSE.magicalUses: 燃燒時,乳香會釋放出強大的震動,不僅可以提升所在區域的活
FRANKINCENSE.lore: One of the gifts the Magi brought to the infant Jesus; ancient Egyptians burned it at sunrise as an offering to Ra.

FUMITORY.magicalUses: 在房子周圍噴灑球果紫堇的浸劑,並且每週用這個浸劑擦一次鞋 子，能夠快速招財。
FUMITORY.lore: Its Latin name 'fumus terrae' means 'smoke of the earth'; medieval exorcists burned it to drive out evil spirits.

FUZZY.magicalUses: 這種植物和艾蒿與艾草是同一屬, 美洲印第安人會用來於吸引爱情,只要將其摩擦在衣服和身體上,即可產生
FUZZY.lore: Tarragon's species name 'dracunculus' means 'little dragon'; French tarragon is essential to béarnaise sauce and was used to cure snakebites.

GALANGAL.magicalUses: 高良薑用於许多不同的魔法需求。穿戴或攜帶會產生保護作 用，還能吸引好運。舆銀放在一個皮革香包中，能夠招財。燃燒磨成粉的高 良薑,可以破除咒語和詛咒。擕帶或灑在家中,會提升慾望。
GALANGAL.lore: A key spice in medieval European cuisine; Hildegard von Bingen called it the 'spice of life' and prescribed it for heart ailments.

GARDENIA.magicalUses: 将新鮮花朵放置在病房，或是為了治療而擺設的祭壇上，有助於 療癒過程的進行。
GARDENIA.lore: Named after Scottish-American naturalist Alexander Garden; in the Victorian language of flowers, it means 'secret love.'

GARLIC.ritualUses: 在膜拜女神赫卡特的慶典期間會吃大蒜,並將大蒜留在十字路 口，以袍的名義獻祭。
GARLIC.magicalUses: 大蒜曾用來對抗瘟疫,至今仍然用於吸收疾病。只需將新鮮去皮 的大蒜瓣搗碎,塗抹在身體受影響的部位,然後將其丢入流動的水中。
GARLIC.lore: Ancient Egyptian pyramid builders were given garlic daily for strength; legend says it repels vampires from Eastern European folklore.

GENTIAN.magicalUses: 黃龍膽可添加在具爱情作用的洗浴和香包中。若添加在任何類 型的薰香或香包中，黄龍膽會增加大量額外的力量。
GENTIAN.lore: Named after King Gentius of Illyria (180 BCE), who discovered its medicinal properties; alpine gentian is a symbol of Bavaria.

GERANIUM.magicalUses: 所有種在花園中,或是新鮮採下帶回家中並插在水裡的天竺 葵，都具有保護作用。
GERANIUM.lore: The Victorians used geraniums to send coded messages in the language of flowers; a scarlet geranium means 'comfort.'

GINSENG.magicalUses: 攜帶花旗參的根能吸引爱情,還能守護個人健康、招財,並且確 保性能力。
GINSENG.lore: In Chinese medicine, ginseng's human-shaped root led to beliefs it could rejuvenate the whole body; it has been used for over 5,000 years.

GOAT'S.magicalUses: 在治療儀式中會用到山羊豆。将山羊豆的葉子放入鞋中，可治療 並預防風濕病。
GOAT'S.lore: Used in Europe since the Middle Ages to increase milk production; it contains a compound related to metformin.

GOLDENROD.magicalUses: 要看到未來的爱人,戴上一枝黃花,他或她將會在明天現身。
GOLDENROD.lore: Thomas Edison experimented with goldenrod to produce rubber; Native Americans used it as a wound healer and divining rod.

GOLDEN.magicalUses: 金印草多用於金錢法術以及治療儀式中。
GOLDEN.lore: Cherokee people called it 'yellow root'; overharvesting has made it endangered in the wild.

G ORSE.magicalUses: 荊豆是對抗邪惡的極佳保護藥草。在威爾斯,多刺的荊豆籬笆可
G ORSE.lore: Celtic tradition says gorse never goes out of season — 'When gorse is out of bloom, kissing is out of fashion.'

GOTU.magicalUses: 用於冥想薰香。在冥想之前(但不是在冥想期間)燃烧一點。
GOTU.lore: Sri Lankan legend says elephants eat gotu kola for longevity, earning it the name 'elephant herb.'

GOURD.magicalUses: 將南瓜掛在前門會有保護作用,可抵抗邪惡。可將切片的南瓜放 在口袋或錢包中，有避邪的作用。
GOURD.lore: One of the earliest domesticated plants, used as containers and musical instruments long before they were eaten.

GRAIN.magicalUses: 要保護自己抵禦邪惡,可在臥室四 周處撒穀物種子。
GRAIN.lore: Medieval Europeans used these West African seeds as a pepper substitute; the name evokes the mythical Garden of Eden.

GRAINS.magicalUses: 天堂籽多運用於愛情、悠望、運氣和金錢的法，以及這類型的 香包中。
GRAINS.lore: Medieval Europeans used these West African seeds as a pepper substitute; the name evokes the mythical Garden of Eden.

GRAPE.magicalUses: 就像古羅馬時代，在花園的牆[壁塗上]釀酒葡萄的圆像，可確保豐 收。吃釀酒釀酒葡萄或釀酒葡萄乾可以增加生育力,並增強精神力量。
GRAPE.lore: Dionysus/Bacchus gave humanity the grapevine; Noah planted a vineyard as his first act after the Great Flood.

GRASS.magicalUses: 在家的前窗掛一把綠草，可以驅邪 並保護居家環境。在家裡的草地上將草打結, 也可以達到為同様效果。
GRASS.lore: In Celtic tradition, offering someone a blade of grass was a peace gesture; Walt Whitman's 'Leaves of Grass' celebrates its universality.

GROUND.magicalUses: 可利用金錢薄荷來找出是誰對你施以惡意的魔法。將藥草放在黃
GROUND.lore: Ground ivy was used to clarify and flavor ale before hops took over; brewers called it 'alehoof.'

GROUNDSEL.magicalUses: 將欧洲黄菀攜帶在身上,可作為對抗牙痛的護身符,也可以在疼 痛一開始時發揮止痛作用。一般來說,攜帶它也有保健牙齒的作用。
GROUNDSEL.lore: Ground ivy was used to clarify and flavor ale before hops took over; brewers called it 'alehoof.'

HAWTHORN.ritualUses: 過去山楂曾用來装飾五朔節花柱( May poles)。 山楂曾經被認 為是女巫幻化成的樹。
HAWTHORN.magicalUses: 很久以前就知道山楂可用來強化生育力，由於具有這種力量，因 此會在婚禮中使用，特别是在春天舉行的婚禮。
HAWTHORN.lore: Sacred to Celtic May Day celebrations; it is taboo in Irish folklore to cut a lone hawthorn — they are fairy meeting places.

HAZEL.magicalUses: 把榛果串起來,掛在屋裡會帶來好運,送给新娘一堆榛果,也能 祝福她好運。
HAZEL.lore: Celtic druids used hazel rods for divination; in Irish mythology, the Salmon of Wisdom ate hazelnuts that fell into a sacred pool.

HEATHER.magicalUses: 攜帶帚石楠可防強姦犯和其他暴力罪犯,或者純粹只是為增加好
HEATHER.lore: In Scottish tradition, white heather brings good luck; Queen Victoria popularized this belief after Prince Albert picked her a sprig.

HELIOTROPE.magicalUses: 将天芥菜放在枕頭下方，能夠誘發預言夢境，這在遭遇搶劫時尤
HELIOTROPE.lore: In Greek myth, the nymph Clytie was turned into this sun-following flower after being abandoned by the sun god Helios.

HELLEBORE,BLACK.magicalUses: 行動前先撒一些聖誕玫瑰的粉末，能夠隱形。在過去，聖誕玫瑰 也用於驅魔儀式，以及引發靈魂出竅。
HELLEBORE,BLACK.lore: The 'Christmas rose' blooms in winter; ancient Greeks used it to cure madness and as a chemical weapon in warfare.

HEMLOCK.magicalUses: 毒参是魔法中另一種用來誘導靈魂來保護的藥草，也用於消除性
HEMLOCK.lore: The philosopher Socrates was executed by drinking hemlock tea in 399 BCE — one of history's most famous poisonings.

HEMP.nameZh: 以便在使用前賦予它們能大麻
HEMP.magicalUses: 大麻曾在魔法中廣泛被運用,但由於在一九三〇年代頒布了使用 和銷售禁令，許多相關法術於是渐漸為人所遺忘，以下是一些例子。
HEMP.lore: One of humanity's oldest cultivated plants, with archaeological evidence of hemp use dating back 10,000 years in Taiwan.

HENBANE.magicalUses: 在今天的藥草魔法中，這是另一種因為其毒性而幾乎為人所遗忘 的有毒植物。今日，天仙子有時仍會用作愛情魔藥,使用方式如下：要獲得 愛情,一個男人必須在早晨時裸體,並且單腳站立地採集天仙子。然後將其 穿戴在身上，便能得到愛情。
HENBANE.lore: Shakespeare likely referenced henbane as the poison poured into King Hamlet's ear; it has been used as an anesthetic since ancient Egypt.

HENNA.magicalUses: 放在額頭上，能夠缓解頭痛。若 是穿戴在心臓附近，可吸引愛情。
HENNA.lore: Cleopatra dyed her hair with henna; the tradition of bridal mehndi (henna tattoos) dates back over 5,000 years in South Asia.

HIBISCUS.magicalUses: 將紅色的朱槿花泡成濃烈的紅色茶汁,飲用後會產生慾望所引發 的力量。基於這個原因，在埃及是禁止女性飲用這種飲料。
HIBISCUS.lore: The national flower of Malaysia and South Korea; in Hawaiian culture, wearing a hibiscus behind the left ear means you're taken.

HICKORY.magicalUses: 將一塊山核桃根燒成灰燼,與五葉
HICKORY.lore: Andrew Jackson's nickname 'Old Hickory' reflected American frontier reverence for the tree's toughness and resilience.

HIGH.magicalUses: 用薄荷油塗抹藥喇叭的一條根,並用綠色香包紮起來,攜帶在身 上，可招財。
HIGH.lore: Central to African American Hoodoo tradition, this root symbolizes overcoming adversity and was carried by enslaved people for hope.

HOLLY.magicalUses: 這是一種保護效果極佳的藥草，能夠抵禦閃電、毒藥和邪靈。種 植在家中,能夠保護居家環境和當中的居住者,免受惡作劇的巫師騷擾。
HOLLY.lore: Pre-Christian Europeans decorated with holly at Yule to shelter woodland spirits; its evergreen leaves symbolize eternal life.

HONESTY.magicalUses: 隨身攜帶銀扇草,或者將其撒在一個你想施法的地方,能夠驅除 所有的怪物。
HONESTY.lore: Named for its translucent seed pods ('silver dollars'); medieval Europeans grew it as a symbol of truthfulness.

HONEYSUCKLE.magicalUses: 將忍冬花繞在綠色蠟燭旁,可招財;擺在房子裡的花瓶內也有同 様效果。輕輕壓碎鮮花，在額頭上摩擦，可提高靈力。
HONEYSUCKLE.lore: In the Victorian language of flowers, honeysuckle means 'bonds of love'; its sweet nectar has been sipped by children for centuries.

HOPS.magicalUses: 將乾燥的蛇麻花塞满枕頭,可讓人好眠和休息。
HOPS.lore: Before hops, medieval brewers used a mix called 'gruit' to flavor beer; hops won out partly because they helped preserve the drink.

HOREHOUND.ritualUses: 因為會燒給古埃及神荷魯斯，所以這植物的英文名稱便來自於袍 的名號。
HOREHOUND.magicalUses: 歐夏至草多應用於製作保護型香包,攜帶在身上,可以對抗巫術 和迷術。
HOREHOUND.lore: One of the oldest known cough remedies; ancient Egyptians called it 'seed of Horus' and used it against poison.

HORSE.magicalUses: 攜帶馬栗可避免風濕、背痛、關節炎和發冷。攜帶三顆在身 上，可防止眩量。
HORSE.lore: Turkish cavalry fed horse chestnuts to winded horses; the game of 'conkers' has been played with them since the 1800s.

HORSERADISH.magicalUses: 將辣根(乾燥或磨碎的)撒在房屋周圍、角落、戶外臺階和門檻 上，便能清除所有邪恶的力量，並反轉任何施加於你的法術。
HORSERADISH.lore: The Oracle at Delphi told Apollo that horseradish was worth its weight in gold; it remains a Passover Seder staple.

HORSETAIL.magicalUses: 吹以木賊的莖製成的口哨，能夠召唤蛇到身邊來。
HORSETAIL.lore: A living fossil — horsetail's ancestors grew as tall as trees 350 million years ago in the Carboniferous period.

HOUNDSTONGUE.magicalUses: 將紅花琉璃草放入鞋中,可阻止狗對你吠叫,實際上這是「捆 綁」住牠們的舌頭。
HOUNDSTONGUE.lore: Named for its rough, tongue-shaped leaves; medieval herbalists used it for dog bites following the Doctrine of Signatures.

HOUSELEEK.magicalUses: 若是種在屋頂上，可帶來好運,還能避免建築遭到雷撃。
HOUSELEEK.lore: Charlemagne ordered houseleek planted on every roof to protect against lightning; it still grows on European cottage roofs today.

HUCKLEBERRY.magicalUses: 將歐洲越橘的葉子放在香包中隨身攜帶,可以誘導好運氣的來 臨。它們也能驅邪，並且打破詛咒和咒語。
HUCKLEBERRY.lore: Mark Twain's Huckleberry Finn was named after this humble berry; 'huckleberry' in American slang means a perfectly matched companion.

HYACINTH.magicalUses: 用於製作香包，可舒缓分娩時的痛 苦。在臥室裡種這種植物,可避免做噩夢。
HYACINTH.lore: In Greek myth, the flower sprang from the blood of the youth Hyacinthus, accidentally killed by Apollo with a discus.

HYDRANGEA.magicalUses: 攜帶、撒在家中,或是燃燒繡球花
HYDRANGEA.lore: In Japan, hydrangeas are associated with gratitude and apology; the flower's color changes based on soil pH — a natural litmus test.

HYSSOP.magicalUses: 在魔法中,牛膝草廣泛用於純化,會將其香包放在澡盆中,以浸 泡或噴撒的方式,作用在物體或人身上,使其潔淨。掛在家中,能清除邪惡
HYSSOP.lore: Psalm 51 says 'Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean'; one of the most ancient purification herbs in Western tradition.

INDIAN.magicalUses: 火焰草的花朵具有強大的爱情吸引力,要尋找愛人,應當攜帶這
INDIAN.lore: Corn/maize was sacred to countless Native American peoples as one of the 'Three Sisters' alongside squash and beans.

IRIS.magicalUses: 尾花是一種愛情花，自羅馬時代起就用於淨化，将鮮花置於待 清潔的區域即可。
IRIS.lore: Named after the Greek goddess Iris, who used rainbows as bridges between heaven and earth; the fleur-de-lis is a stylized iris.

IRISH.ritualUses: 崇拜巴克斯的權杖上經常會以常春藤纏繞。
IRISH.magicalUses: 隨身攜帶鹿角菜或將其放置在地毯下方,可增添運氣,確保錢財 穩定流入房屋或口袋。
IRISH.lore: During the Irish Potato Famine, coastal communities survived on this seaweed; it remains popular in Caribbean drinks.

JASMINE.magicalUses: 乾燥的茉莉花可加在香包和其他爱情類的混合藥草中,這會吸引 精神性(而非肉體的)爱情。
JASMINE.lore: In India, jasmine garlands welcome honored guests; Persian poets called it 'moonlight of the grove' for its luminous white flowers.

JOB'S.magicalUses: 将其種子串成項錬戴在孩子的脖子 上,可以幫助孩子長牙,成人帶著能舒緩喉嚨
JOB'S.lore: Named after the biblical Job; in Southeast Asia, these hard seeds have been used as beads and currency for thousands of years.

JOE-PYE.magicalUses: 想要愛情有所進展，在嘴理含幾片紫澤蘭葉子會有所幫助，應當
JOE-PYE.lore: Named after a Native American healer who used it to treat typhoid fever among colonial settlers.

JUNIPER.magicalUses: 在整個歐洲都用作保護型的藥草,杜松有也防盜功能。
JUNIPER.lore: One of the most ancient protective plants; burning juniper to cleanse spaces is documented in Sumerian texts over 4,000 years old.

KAVA-KAVA.ritualUses: 在夏威夷和玻里尼希亞,長久以來都應用於儀式中。
KAVA-KAVA.magicalUses: 這種玻里尼希亞植物的根可用來浸泡，飲用其茶湯,能獲得保 護、抵禦邪恶，還能招來好運。
KAVA-KAVA.lore: Pacific Islander chiefs have drunk kava ceremonially for 3,000 years; it plays a role similar to wine in Mediterranean cultures.

KELP.lore: The underwater forests of giant kelp can grow up to 2 feet per day; they shelter some of the richest marine ecosystems on Earth.

KNOTWEED.magicalUses: 手裡拿著一些萹蓄,可將困境和苦難「束縛」起來。把問題送入 藥草，想像它為篇蓄吸收，然後将其燒掉。
KNOTWEED.lore: Shakespeare mentions 'hindering knotgrass' in A Midsummer Night's Dream as a plant that stunts growth.

LADY'S.magicalUses: 用於愛情法術和這類型的香包。
LADY'S.lore: Alchemists collected morning dew from its pleated leaves, believing it held the key to the Philosopher's Stone.

LARCH.magicalUses: 根據長久以來的魔法傳統,火無 法燒過歐洲落葉松的木材，因此會用於避免 爆炸型的香包。
LARCH.lore: The larch is one of few deciduous conifers; Siberian shamans considered it a tree bridging the living and spirit worlds.

LARKSPUR.magicalUses: 翠雀可讓鬼魂遠離。若是在仲夏的火中看到一堆翠雀，那麽眼睛 就會受到保護,直到來年的仲夏。
LARKSPUR.lore: In Greek myth, larkspur grew from the blood of Ajax; its seeds were once used to make ink for magical writing.

LAVENDER.magicalUses: 長久以來,薰衣草一直用於愛情魔法和香包。沾有花香的衣服 (或是將薰衣草放在衣服抽屜裡),可吸引爱情。以薰衣草摩擦的紙張,非 常適合用來寫情書。薰衣草的香味特別能吸引男性,幾個世紀前的妓女,多 會噴撒薰衣草水或精油,宣傳其專業,同時也吸引(透過魔法)顧客。如果 在手上抹薰衣草，也可以防止配偶残暴對待。
LAVENDER.lore: Roman soldiers washed with lavender (from Latin 'lavare' — to wash); it was strewn on medieval castle floors for fragrance and pest control.

LEE.magicalUses: 當兩人一起吃韭蒽時會陷入情網,因此韭蒽也用作保護型的護身
LEE.lore: The leek is the national emblem of Wales; according to legend, Welsh soldiers wore leeks in battle to distinguish friend from foe.

LEMON.magicalUses: 將檸檬汁與水混合,所得的汁液可用來清洗護身符、珠寶和其他
LEMON.lore: Arab traders introduced lemons to Europe; British sailors ate them to prevent scurvy, earning the nickname 'limeys.'

LEMONGRASS.magicalUses: 在家中和花園裡種植檸檬香茅可驅蛇。這也用於製作一些慾望魔 藥 ,以及可幫助發展靈力的浸劑。
LEMONGRASS.lore: Used in traditional Ayurvedic medicine for centuries; in the Philippines, it is called 'tanglad' and is both culinary and magical.

LETTUCE.magicalUses: 用蒿苣菜汁來摩擦額頭或是直接吃食蒿苣的葉子，就不會有失眠 的問題。
LETTUCE.lore: Ancient Egyptians associated lettuce with the fertility god Min; the milky sap was linked to virility.

LICORICE.magicalUses: 咀嚼甘草棒(是甘草的根而不是 一 般的甘草糖)會讓你充满熱 情 。 這也是戒的好方法 。
LICORICE.lore: Found in Tutankhamun's tomb; Alexander the Great's troops chewed licorice root on long marches to quench thirst.

LIFE-EVERLASTING.magicalUses: 用於長壽法術,以及恢復青春。存放在家中或是隨身攜帶,可預 防疾病及健康問题。
LIFE-EVERLASTING.lore: Also called 'immortelle'; its flowers retain their shape and color when dried, symbolizing eternal life in folk magic.

LILAC.magicalUses: 種植或散落紫丁香的地方能夠驅邪，事實上，當初在新英格蘭地 區種植紫丁香,就是為了避免邪惡進入家園。
LILAC.lore: In the Victorian language of flowers, purple lilac represents the first emotions of love; it is the state flower of New Hampshire.

LILY.magicalUses: 在花園裡種植百合,可驅離鬼魂與邪靈,抵禦邪眼,並阻擋不受 歡迎的訪客上門。
LILY.lore: In Christian iconography, the white lily symbolizes the Virgin Mary's purity; ancient Greeks associated it with Hera's breast milk.

LIME.magicalUses: 取一顆新鮮的萊姆,用舊鐵釘、釘子、別針和繡針刺穿它,然後 扔進地上的深洞裡,這將消除身上所有的疾病和咒語等負面能量。
LIME.lore: British sailors switched from lemons to limes in the 19th century; Columbus brought lime seeds to the New World on his second voyage.

LINDEN.ritualUses: 在過去,立陶宛會將女性獻祭給歐洲椴樹,這是其宗教古老儀式 的一部分。
LINDEN.magicalUses: 歐洲椴樹在歐洲廣泛用作保護樹。將樹枝懸掛在門上,或是種在 花園裡,也同樣有保護的效果。
LINDEN.lore: In Germanic tradition, the linden was the tree of lovers and justice; village courts often convened under linden trees.

LIQUIDAMBER.magicalUses: 為了對抗邪惡勢力求得保護,會在祭壇上放置其豆莢,或是在魔 法儀式期間拿在手上。
LIQUIDAMBER.lore: Ancient Maya and Aztec peoples used liquidambar resin as incense and medicine; the fragrant gum was one of the tribute items demanded by Aztec rulers.

LIVERWORT.lore: Named for its liver-shaped leaves; the Doctrine of Signatures led herbalists to prescribe it for liver complaints.
LIVERWORT.magicalUses: Carried for love and protection. Used in sachets for healing.

LOBELIA.magicalUses: 女人可以隨時攜帶加入地錢的香包,來鞏固男人對她的愛情。
LOBELIA.lore: Named after Flemish botanist Matthias de Lobel; Native Americans smoked it as a tobacco substitute, calling it 'Indian tobacco.'

LOOSESTRIFE.magicalUses: 要解決和朋友的爭吵，给他或她一些這種藥草。 撒在家中,千屈菜會散發和平的震動,排除邪惡的力量。
LOOSESTRIFE.lore: Pliny the Elder wrote that placing loosestrife on the yoke of quarrelsome oxen would calm them — its very name means 'ending strife.'

LOTUS.ritualUses: 在東方,長久以來視蓮花為生命、靈性和宇宙中心的神秘象 徵 。古埃及人認為這種植物是神聖的，會将蓮花獻祭給神靈。
LOTUS.magicalUses: 任何聞到蓮花香味的人，都會得到它的保護。
LOTUS.lore: In ancient Egypt, the blue lotus symbolized rebirth and the sun; in Buddhism and Hinduism, it represents spiritual purity rising from muddy waters.

LOVAGE.magicalUses: 將圓葉當歸放在洗澡水中(置於 一 香包內),會讓人更有吸引
LOVAGE.lore: Roman legionnaires planted lovage throughout their empire; medieval travelers tucked it in their shoes to soothe tired feet.

LOVE.magicalUses: 爪哇的印第安人會在其魔法中使用這種藥草。攜帶這藥草會吸引
LOVE.lore: Prized in folk love magic for its sympathetic properties; carried in sachets to attract romantic attention.

LUCKY.magicalUses: 這種蘭花植物的根，是美國新奥爾良地區一種非常著名的魔法植 物。長久以來都用作香包和召唤袋的材料,以求得好運和普遍的成功,攜帶 在身上,有利於找工作與持續就業,還有保護作用,不致疾病纏身。
LUCKY.lore: This orchid root naturally resembles a hand with fingers; in Hoodoo, it is one of the most powerful gambling charms.

MACE.lore: Mace and nutmeg come from the same fruit; during the Age of Exploration, nutmeg was more valuable than gold by weight.
MACE.magicalUses: Burned to increase psychic powers. Added to sachets for mental clarity and carried for luck in gambling.

MAGUEY.magicalUses: 燃燒肉荳蔻的假種皮,可增加靈力;隨身攜帶,可提高智力。
MAGUEY.lore: The Aztec goddess Mayahuel personified the maguey plant; pulque made from its sap was the sacred drink of Mesoamerica.

MAGNOLIA.lore: One of the most ancient flowering plants, predating bees by millions of years; it evolved to be pollinated by beetles instead.
MAGNOLIA.magicalUses: Placed near the bed or under the pillow to maintain a faithful relationship. The bark and flowers are used in fidelity spells.

MAHOGANY.magicalUses: 在床的下方或附近放一些洋玉蘭,可與伴侶維持忠诚的關係。
MAHOGANY.lore: Spanish colonizers prized mahogany so highly that they called it 'the wood of the gods'; it became the preferred timber for European royalty's furniture.

MAIDENHAIR.magicalUses: 將一些鐵線蕨浸泡在水中,然後取出。之後若是穿戴在身上或留
MAIDENHAIR.lore: Its genus 'Adiantum' means 'unwetted' — water rolls right off its fronds, which medieval herbalists found magical.

MALE.magicalUses: 歐洲鱗毛蕨是一種強大的運氣誘發劑,也會吸引女性。
MALE.lore: Ancient herbalists believed this fern could make you invisible; it was also used against tapeworms since Dioscorides.

MALLOW.magicalUses: 如果是愛人離開,採一把錦葵放在門外(或窗户旁)的花瓶
MALLOW.lore: The original marshmallow was made from mallow root; ancient Romans considered mallow a delicacy and placed it on their tables daily.

MANDRAKE.magicalUses: 將整株曼德拉草的根置於家中的壁爐架上,可以為房屋裡的人帶 來保護、生育力和繁榮。
MANDRAKE.lore: One of the most legendary magical plants; its human-shaped root was said to scream when pulled from the ground, killing anyone who heard it.

MAPLE.magicalUses: 槭樹的葉子會用於愛情和金錢的魔法與儀式中，其枝條長久以來 都是製作魔杖的材料。
MAPLE.lore: The maple leaf became Canada's symbol; Native Americans were the first to tap maple trees for syrup, teaching colonists the technique.

MARIGOLD.magicalUses: 在正中午陽光最熱和最強的時候所採摘的金盏花，能強化和安撫 心臟。
MARIGOLD.lore: The Aztecs considered marigolds flowers of the dead; Mexico's Día de los Muertos altars are still adorned with them.
