MARJORAM.magicalUses: 在愛情魔咒中會用到馬鬱蘭,也會加在食物中強化爱情。
MARJORAM.lore: Greek myth says Aphrodite grew marjoram; the word 'oregano' comes from Greek meaning 'joy of the mountain.'

MASTERWORT.magicalUses: 將歐前胡穿戴在身上,能夠增加體力,因此許多勞動者和運動員 會利用它來強化身體。
MASTERWORT.lore: Highly valued in Alpine folk medicine; Paracelsus himself praised masterwort as a panacea for mountain communities.

MASTIC.magicalUses: 在施法時燃燒薰陸香,便能將願望顯靈而出。
MASTIC.lore: Harvested on the Greek island of Chios for over 2,500 years; the word 'masticate' (to chew) comes from this ancient chewing gum.

MAY.magicalUses: 鬼臼，或是許多種蘋果，通常會用作歐洲(真正的)曼德拉草的
MAY.lore: Named for the month it blooms; may apple's umbrella-like leaves sheltered a single fruit the Cherokee used medicinally.

MEADOW.magicalUses: 美國印第安人會將其戴在脖子上,當作萬用護身符,攜帶在身上
MEADOW.lore: Named for its habitat; meadow rue is unrelated to true rue despite sharing a common name.

folkNames: Br id e of the Meadow
MEADOWSWEET.magicalUses: 在施行爱情法術時,會將新鮮的旋果蚊子草放在祭壇上,乾燥花
MEADOWSWEET.lore: One of the three most sacred herbs of the Druids; aspirin was originally synthesized from chemicals found in meadowsweet.

MESQUITE.lore: Native Americans of the Southwest depended on mesquite pods as a dietary staple; the wood gives BBQ its distinctive smoky flavor.
MESQUITE.magicalUses: Added to healing and purifying incenses. The wood is burned for cleansing spaces.

MIMOSA.magicalUses: 會加到治療型的薰香和混合藥草中，也用作魔法火焰的燃料。
MIMOSA.lore: The sensitive plant (Mimosa pudica) closes its leaves when touched — Charles Darwin studied this behavior and called it 'plant intelligence.'

MINT.magicalUses: 薄荷長久以來被用於治療型的魔藥和混合藥草中，以新鮮葉子摩 擦頭部,可舒緩頭痛。将薄荷擦拭在手腕上,可確保不會生病。将薄荷填裝 在人偶中,並用治療油塗抹它,可以緩解胃部問題。
MINT.lore: In Greek myth, the nymph Minthe was transformed into this plant by Persephone; Romans crowned themselves with peppermint at feasts.

MISTLETOE.ritualUses: 眾所周知,德魯伊人( Druids) 崇敬槲寄生,特別是長在橡樹上 的。過去,他們會在仲夏那天(現在仍然是)或是在新月算起的第六天將其 切下。在以前，會用金鐮刀來砍，而且禁止讓槲寄生碰觸到地面。
MISTLETOE.magicalUses: 長久以來,槲寄生被用於抵抗雷擊、疾病,以及各種不幸事故與 火災等,可攜帶或是放置在適當地方,便能發揮這種用途。葉子和漿果都會 用到 。
MISTLETOE.lore: The Druids cut mistletoe from oak with a golden sickle at the winter solstice; the kissing tradition comes from Norse mythology.

MOLUKKA.magicalUses: 将白色的摩魯卡堅果掛在脖子上，可以顯示及破除魔咒和詛
MOLUKKA.lore: Named after the Moluccas (Spice Islands) of Indonesia; its papery calyx was used as a natural lantern in tropical folk traditions.

MOONWORT.magicalUses: 將陰地蕨放在盒子和袋子中,據說會出現銀子。這一直是用於所 有類型的金錢法術。
MOONWORT.lore: Alchemists believed moonwort could open locks and unshoe horses that stepped on it; its crescent-shaped fronds connect it to the moon.

MORNING.magicalUses: 將牽牛花種子放在枕頭下,就不會再做噩夢。 在花園裡種植藍色牽牛花,能夠帶來平安和幸福。
MORNING.lore: The Aztecs used morning glory seeds in divination ceremonies; they contain LSA, a natural psychoactive compound.

MOSS.magicalUses: 在口袋中放入從從墓碑上取下的苔 蘚 (任何類型) ,保證能帶來好運,特別是錢 財方面的運氣。
MOSS.lore: In Japanese garden design, moss represents age, tranquility, and the passage of time; Saihoji temple has over 120 moss varieties.

MUGWORT.magicalUses: 将艾草置於鞋中，便可以在長途步行或跑步時獲得力氣。為
MUGWORT.lore: One of the Anglo-Saxon Nine Herbs Charm, called 'mother of herbs'; Roman soldiers put mugwort in their sandals for endurance.

MULBERRY.magicalUses: 桑樹可保護花園免受雷擊。在以意志力作用時,它也有所幫 助，因其木材是對抗邪恶的強大保護者。可製作成魔杖。
MULBERRY.lore: In Chinese legend, the mulberry tree connects heaven and earth; silkworms feed exclusively on its leaves, making it central to the Silk Road.

MUSTARD,BLACK.magicalUses: 印度教徒會使用黑芥末籽在空中穿梭。較為一般的用途，是在紅
MUSTARD,BLACK.lore: Jesus's Parable of the Mustard Seed appears in three Gospels; ancient Romans ground mustard with grape juice to make the first prepared mustard.

MYRRH.ritualUses: 在古埃及，會於正午時分燃燒没藥樹,獻給太陽神拉，也會在生 育之神艾西斯的神廟中焚燒。
MYRRH.magicalUses: 燃燒没藥製成的薰香，可淨化一區域，移走振動,帶來平和。不 過很少會單獨燃燒沒藥,通常會與乳香或其他樹脂一起使用。沒藥會增加所 有焚香類型的力量。也會加入治療型的薰香和香包中，其煙霧用於聖化、淨 化和祝福護身符、法寶、符咒和魔法用具等物品。没藥也有助於冥想和沉
MYRRH.lore: One of the gifts the Magi brought to the infant Jesus; ancient Egyptians burned myrrh at noon as an offering to Ra.

MYRTLE.magicalUses: 香桃木一直以來都被當成是「爱情」藥草,在施行爱情法術 時,很適合將新鮮的葉子和花朵戴在頭上。
MYRTLE.lore: Sacred to Aphrodite/Venus; ancient Greek brides wore myrtle wreaths, and Queen Victoria carried myrtle in her wedding bouquet in 1840.

NETTLE.magicalUses: 蓐麻的保護力長久以來一直用於魔 法。要解除詛咒,並將其返送回去,可用蕁麻 填充人偶,或是放一些在香包中,随身攜带。
NETTLE.lore: Tibetans say the sage Milarepa survived on nettle soup during his years of cave meditation, turning green from the diet.

NORFOLK.lore: Not actually a pine; Captain Cook discovered it on Norfolk Island in 1774 and thought the trees would make ship masts.
NORFOLK.magicalUses: Placed in the home for protection against hunger and poverty. Used as a living protective charm.

NUTMEG.magicalUses: 在家中或附近種此植物,能發揮保護作用,抵抗飢餓和邪惡。
NUTMEG.lore: In the 1667 Treaty of Breda, the Dutch ceded Manhattan to England in exchange for control of the nutmeg-producing island of Run in the Banda Islands.

NUTS.magicalUses: 所有堅果都是強效的生育誘導物，
NUTS.lore: Across many traditions, nuts symbolize hidden wisdom — a hard shell protecting something precious within, much like esoteric knowledge.

OAK.ritualUses: 由於白爍木是英國和歐洲早期定居者的食物來源，在史前時代就
OAK.magicalUses: 像白櫟木這樣長壽和強壯的樹,會自然地提供魔法的保護。將兩 根樹枝以紅線捆綁,做成一個等臂的十字架,便是對抗邪惡的強力保障,應 该将其掛在房子裡。
OAK.lore: Sacred to Zeus, Thor, and the Druids; the word 'druid' may derive from the Celtic word for oak, 'dru.'

OATS.magicalUses: 用於發達和金錢類型的法術。
OATS.lore: Samuel Johnson mocked oats as 'food for horses in England and people in Scotland'; the Scots retorted, 'And that's why England has such fine horses.'

OLEANDER.magicalUses: 雖然義大利魔藥學認為,在家中保留夾竹桃的任何一部分，都會 給家人帶來各種疾病、恥辱和不幸,但夾竹桃偶爾也會用在爱情法術中,只 是絕對不能内服。
OLEANDER.lore: Despite its deadly toxicity, oleander lines Mediterranean roads beautifully; legend says Hannibal's soldiers fell ill from roasting meat on oleander sticks.

OLIVE.ritualUses: 在遠古時代，會在燈具中燃燒這種油，照亮神廟。
OLIVE.magicalUses: 在橄欖葉上寫下雅典娜的名字，然後在頭上按壓,或穿在身 上 , 可治頭痛。長久以來,橄欖油都被當作是用來輔助治療的塗抹膏油。
OLIVE.lore: Athena won patronage of Athens by gifting the olive tree; some olive trees in the Garden of Gethsemane are over 2,000 years old.

ONION.ritualUses: 根據一些古老權威人士的説法，在古埃及的一些城市會崇拜洋 蒽，有時還會用在宣誓的過程中。
ONION.magicalUses: 取一顆小的白洋蔥,在其上插滿黑頭針,然後放在窗臺上,可防 止邪惡侵入居家。洋蔥花具有裝飾性和保護性,乾燥後放在家中,可獲得非 比尋常且具有吸引力的護身符。隨身擖帶洋蔥能夠抵抗有毒的野獸。種在花 盆或花園裡,也能防禦邪惡。
ONION.lore: Ancient Egyptians swore oaths on onions; their concentric layers symbolized eternity, and onions were placed in mummy wrappings.

ORANGE.magicalUses: 乾燥的果皮和種子會加到爱情類型的香包中，而加入橙花的香 包，是設計來祝福結婚的。在浴缸中加入的新鮮或乾燥的花朵，能使沐浴者 更具吸引力。
ORANGE.lore: The orange blossom tradition at weddings began in China and spread to Europe via the Moors; it symbolizes purity and fertility.

ORCHID.magicalUses: 長久以來,蘭花一直用於愛情法愆，尤其是根部，會放在香包中 攜带 。
ORCHID.lore: The name comes from Greek 'orchis' (testicle), due to the shape of its root tubers; Aztec nobles flavored their chocolate with vanilla orchid.

OREGON.magicalUses: 擴帶其根部,能招財,還能鞏固財務安全、增加人氣。
OREGON.lore: Oregon grape is the state flower of Oregon; Native Americans of the Pacific Northwest used its bright yellow root as dye and medicine.

ORRIS.magicalUses: 鳶尾的根長久以來就用來尋找及擁有愛情。可攜帶整條鳶尾 根,或將其粉末加入香包,或撒在床單、衣服和身體上及房子的周圍。鳶尾 根的粉有時稱為「愛情粉」 (D rawing Love Powder)。
ORRIS.lore: Made from iris root, orris powder was used in Elizabethan England to scent linens and wigs; it takes five years to develop its violet scent.

PALM,DATE.magicalUses: 椰棗樹因為會産生大量的果實,以其生育力著名。因此，會佩戴 或攜帶椰棗或其樹葉的碎片,或是吃椰棗,藉以增加生育力。希望恢復性能 力的男性則會带其籽。
PALM,DATE.lore: Date palms have fed Middle Eastern peoples for 6,000 years; they appear over 20 times in the Quran.

PANSY.magicalUses: 佩帶或攜帶三色堇,能招來愛情。在爱情占卜中也很有效用。将 三色董排列成心形來種植，若是長得茂盛，你的愛情也會如此。
PANSY.lore: The name comes from French 'pensée' (thought); in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, pansy juice causes love at first sight.

PAPAYA.magicalUses: 長久以來,木瓜常被用於魔法儀式中，其中最簡單的是在一棵木 瓜樹上繫上一塊碎布,同時在腦中想像你的需要,願望即可達成。
PAPAYA.lore: Christopher Columbus called it the 'fruit of the angels'; its enzyme papain can tenderize meat and was used to shrink war trophies.

PAPYRUS.lore: Ancient Egypt's paper was made from papyrus reed; the word 'paper' derives from it, and scrolls have survived over 4,000 years.
PAPYRUS.magicalUses: Used in spells for communication and to discover hidden truths. Burned in divination rituals.

PAROSELA.magicalUses: 放在船上，可防止鱷魚襲撃。
PAROSELA.lore: Used by indigenous peoples of the American Southwest in hunting rituals; the Pima people rubbed it on their bodies before deer hunts.

PARSLEY.magicalUses: 吃下香芹會挑起慾望,促進生育,但如果你是在戀愛中,就不可 切香芹,否則會削減你的愛情。
PARSLEY.lore: Ancient Greeks associated parsley with death and decorated tombs with it; the phrase 'to be in need of parsley' meant someone was near death.

PASSION.magicalUses: 舆其英文名稱中的受難( Passion) 一字正好相反，西番蓮的花放置在房子禅，是 為了以平息纷爭和煩惱,帶來和平。
PASSION.lore: Spanish missionaries named it for Christ's Passion — they saw the crown of thorns, nails, and wounds in its structure.

PATCHOULY.magicalUses: 廣藿香聞起來像是肥沃的土壤，因此會用於金錢和發達類型的混 合藥草和法術。可將其撒在錢上,放入錢包和皮夾中,並且放在綠色蠟燭的 底部。
PATCHOULY.lore: The signature scent of the 1960s counterculture; Indian silk traders packed patchouli leaves with fabrics to repel moths during shipping.

PEA.magicalUses: 脱殻豌豆能為事業帶來財富和利潤,乾燥豌豆則用在金錢類的混
PEA.lore: Gregor Mendel's experiments with pea plants in the 1860s founded the science of genetics.

PEAR.magicalUses: 這種水果會用於愛情法術,也用於引發性煞。
PEAR.lore: Homer called pears 'gifts of the gods' in The Odyssey; the Chinese word for pear (梨) sounds like 'separation,' making it taboo to share.

PECAN.magicalUses: 美洲胡桃會加在所有的金錢和發達類型的法術中。
PECAN.lore: Native Americans stored pecans as a key winter food source; the word comes from Algonquin 'pacaan,' meaning 'nut requiring a stone to crack.'

PENNYROYAL.magicalUses: 將普列薄荷放在鞋子裡,可以防止旅行時的疲倦,同時全方位提 升體力。
PENNYROYAL.lore: Roman naturalist Pliny advised sailors to burn pennyroyal to purify ship water; its name means 'royal thyme.'

PEONY.magicalUses: 從以前到現在，芍藥的保護能力就備受尊崇。穿戴在身上，可保 護身體、精神和靈魂;放在家裡,則可以防止邪靈;種在花園,能夠抵禦邪 惡和風暴。也會將其種子或根掛在孩童的脖子上,以此避免惡作劇的精靈 和小鬼靠近。另一種做法,是將芍藥根雕刻成小珠,稱為「松珠」 ( piney beads), 然後將其串起來。穿戴在身上也具有保護作用。將芍藥根與珊 瑚、燧石一起穿戴，可以防止遭到溺斃。
PEONY.lore: Named after Paeon, physician to the Greek gods, who used it to heal Pluto's wounds; Chinese emperors cultivated peonies as the 'King of Flowers.'

PEPPER.magicalUses: 會將胡椒加到護身符中,當作對抗邪眼的保護劑,穿戴在身,會
PEPPER.lore: Black pepper was so valuable in medieval Europe it was used as currency; Alaric the Goth demanded 3,000 pounds of pepper as ransom for Rome.

PEPPERMINT.magicalUses: 胡椒薄荷長久以來一直用於治療型的魔藥和混合藥草中。
PEPPERMINT.lore: A natural hybrid of watermint and spearmint; ancient Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans all used it medicinally and as a flavoring.

PERIWINKLE.magicalUses: 這是一種強大的魔法藥草(正如其俗名所顯示的，這是「巫師 的紫羅蘭」),採集小蔓長春花必須依循一定的程序,才會具有魔法效 果---至少《世紀羅馬藥草書》是這様記載的。
PERIWINKLE.lore: Medieval Europeans called it 'Sorcerer's Violet'; it was woven into headbands for memory and worn at executions for spiritual protection.

PERSIMMON.magicalUses: 直到最近,在美國阿拉巴馬州都有人相信,要是有女孩想要變成 男孩,只要吃下九顆未成熟的美洲柿,肯定會在兩週內改變性别!
PERSIMMON.lore: In Japanese folklore, a dried persimmon hung by the door brings good fortune; the fruit can only be eaten when fully ripe or it causes intense astringency.

PILOT.lore: Used by travelers as a natural compass plant — its leaves tend to orient north-south, earning the folk name 'compass weed.'
PILOT.magicalUses: Carried by travelers for safe passage and to find their way. Used in direction and guidance spells.

PIMENTO.magicalUses: 在風暴期間,燃燒乾燥過的草根， 可避免閃電。
PIMENTO.lore: Columbus discovered allspice (pimento) in Jamaica, naming it 'pimienta' thinking it was pepper; Jamaican jerk seasoning depends on it.

PIMPERNEL.magicalUses: 带虎耳草茴芹有保護的作用，能防止他人欺騙你。
PIMPERNEL.lore: Called the 'poor man's weather glass' because its flowers close before rain; the fictional Scarlet Pimpernel took his name from this flower.

PINE.magicalUses: 攜帶松樹的毬果可增加生育力,並可擁有活力十足的晚年。
PINE.lore: Sacred to the Greek god Pan; pine cones appear throughout ancient art as symbols of enlightenment and the pineal gland.

PINEAPPLE.magicalUses: 将鳳梨乾放在小袋中，加到浴缸
PINEAPPLE.lore: A symbol of hospitality since colonial times; captains placed pineapples on their gateposts to announce their safe return.

PIPSISSEWA.magicalUses: 將梅笠草弄碎,與玫瑰果和紫羅蘭的花瓣混合後燃燒,能夠吸引
PIPSISSEWA.lore: The Cree name means 'it breaks into small pieces,' referring to how it was used to break down kidney stones in traditional medicine.

PISTACHIO.magicalUses: 阿拉伯人認為吃開心果,就等於是吃下爱情法術的解藥。拿這種 堅果給殭屍,會使它們脱離恍惚狀態,進入死亡。特別的是,以人工染成的 紅色開心果最適合用來進行這個法術。
PISTACHIO.lore: Queen of Sheba reportedly monopolized Assyria's pistachio harvest; they are one of the oldest flowering nut trees, dating back 80 million years.

PLANTAIN.magicalUses: 用紅色羊毛將車前草綁在頭上,可治療頭痛;放在腳下,則可消 除疲勞。也可將車前草掛在車上，防止邪靈入侵。
PLANTAIN.lore: Called 'white man's footstep' by Native Americans because it appeared wherever European colonists walked.

PLUM.magicalUses: 將歐洲李的枝條放在門上和窗戶上,可保護家庭免受邪惡入 侵。其果實則可用來激發或維持愛情。
PLUM.lore: Confucius meditated under plum trees; in Chinese culture, the plum blossom represents resilience, blooming in winter's harshest cold.

PLUMERIA.magicalUses: 緬梔花多用於愛情魔法中。
PLUMERIA.lore: Called frangipani; in Balinese Hindu tradition, plumeria flowers are essential temple offerings.

POKE.magicalUses: 在新月時,可用垂序商陸來破除詛咒。在家裡製作浸劑,灑在房
POKE.lore: Native Americans used pokeberry juice as ink and dye; the Declaration of Independence may have been drafted in pokeberry ink.

POMEGRANATE.magicalUses: 長久以來人們都以吃石榴的種子來增加生育力,攜帶其果皮也是 基出於同樣的原因。
POMEGRANATE.lore: In Greek myth, Persephone ate pomegranate seeds in the underworld, binding her there for part of each year — creating the seasons.

POPLAR.magicalUses: 攜帶白楊的枝芽和葉子可招財,也可加到金錢類型的薰香中。還
POPLAR.lore: In Greek mythology, Leuce was turned into a white poplar by Hades; its trembling leaves are said to whisper secrets of the dead.

POPPY.magicalUses: 罌粟的種子和花會放在助眠的混合藥草中,也會食用它們來促進 生育力，增添好運和招財。
POPPY.lore: Ancient Minoans worshipped a 'Poppy Goddess'; the Flanders Fields poem made the red poppy a symbol of war remembrance.

POTATO.magicalUses: 馬鈴薯通常會用作人偶以及其他種類的偶的「眼睛」。
POTATO.lore: The Incas freeze-dried potatoes into 'chuño' 2,000 years ago; potatoes were initially rejected in Europe as food fit only for animals.

PRICKLYASH.magicalUses: 美洲花椒的果實可作為吸引愛情的香水。
PRICKLYASH.lore: The prickly ash was called 'toothache tree' by early American settlers; chewing its bark numbs the mouth like a natural anesthetic.

PRIMROSE.magicalUses: 在花園種植蓝色和紅色的歐洲報春花，可以保護花園免受摧 殘,也會吸引精靈。雖然對某些人來説，報春花代表了放縱,但女性會佩戴 它來吸引愛情。
PRIMROSE.lore: In Celtic tradition, placing primroses on doorsteps protects against fairies; the 'primrose path' in Shakespeare means a life of easy pleasure.

P URSLANE.magicalUses: 若是將馬齒莧放在床上,夜間就不會做噩夢。攜帶馬齒莧在身
P URSLANE.lore: Thoreau grew purslane at Walden Pond; it contains more omega-3 fatty acids than any other leafy vegetable and has been eaten for over 4,000 years.

QUASSIA.magicalUses: 苦木會用於愛情混合藥草中,既可吸引也可維持愛情。
QUASSIA.lore: Named after Graman Quassi, an enslaved healer in 18th-century Suriname who discovered its medicinal properties.

QUINCE.ritualUses: 傳說榲桲和許多種神靈都有連結,會用在祭典中,特別是在維納
QUINCE.magicalUses: 攜帶榲桲的種子,可避邪,並預防身體受傷和意外事故。
QUINCE.lore: Many scholars believe the 'golden apple' Paris gave Aphrodite was actually a quince; ancient Greek brides ate quince before the bridal chamber.

RADISH.magicalUses: 攜帶蘿萄可以防止邪眼。食用時,會增加慾望。
RADISH.lore: Ancient Egyptian workers building the pyramids were paid partly in radishes, onions, and garlic.

RAGWEED.magicalUses: 在晚上咀嚼豚草的根部，能驅走所 有的恐懼。
RAGWEED.lore: Though infamous for allergies today, Native Americans used ragweed medicinally for insect bites and fever.

RAGWORT.magicalUses: 希臘人將千里光當作護身符,藉以
RAGWORT.lore: In Irish folklore, fairies ride ragwort stalks like broomsticks; it is also called 'fairy horse.'

RASPBERRY.magicalUses: 將覆盆子的棘(樹枝)掛在門窗上,有保護作用。當家中有人往 生時,也這様做，可確保靈魂離開後不會再進入屋内。
RASPBERRY.lore: Greek myth says raspberries were originally white until the nymph Ida pricked her finger while picking them for the infant Zeus.

RATTLESNAKE.magicalUses: 在洗澡水中加入美遠志根的浸劑, 並且用在冲洗衣服的水中，可抵禦試圖傷害你 的人。
RATTLESNAKE.lore: Named for its use against rattlesnake bites by Native Americans; different plants share this common name by region.

RHUBARB.magicalUses: 在脖子上戴一塊大黄的根，可防止胃痛。
RHUBARB.lore: The Romans imported rhubarb from China along the Silk Road; it was more expensive than opium and cinnamon.

RICE.magicalUses: 將稻米放在屋頂上,可以防止所有的不幸。
RICE.lore: In Japan, the emperor personally plants rice each spring; the word for cooked rice ('gohan') also means 'meal.'

ROOTS.magicalUses: 若是必須在沒有遮蔽的情況下睡在 野外，在脖子上戴上任何一種藥草的根，野生 動物將會保護你。
ROOTS.lore: Root magic is central to many folk traditions worldwide; the shape and growth pattern of roots inspire their magical uses.

ROSE.magicalUses: 玫瑰長久以來一直被用於愛情類型的混合藥草中，因為這種花與 情緒有關。
ROSE.lore: Cleopatra covered the floor in rose petals to greet Mark Antony; Persia's rose gardens inspired the word 'paradise.'

ROSEMARY.magicalUses: 燃燒迷迭香時,會散發出強大的清潔和淨化振動能量，可用來消 除一個充满負面能量的地方,特别是在施法前。這是最古老的一種薰香。
ROSEMARY.lore: Legend says the Virgin Mary draped her cloak over a rosemary bush, turning its white flowers blue; Shakespeare called it the herb of remembrance.

ROWAN.magicalUses: 攜帶歐洲花楸可增加靈力,其樹枝常被做成探棒和魔杖。其葉子 和漿果可添加在占卜類型的薰香中,包括那些企圖增加靈力的部分。
ROWAN.lore: In Celtic tradition, rowan is the strongest protection against enchantment; Scottish farmers made rowan crosses to guard cattle from witchcraft.

RUE.magicalUses: 將芸香的葉子放在額頭上,可舒緩頭痛。戴在脖子上,有助於疾 病的恢復,也可預防未來的健康問題。所以,芸香多添加到治療類型的薰香 和人偶中。
RUE.lore: The Catholic Church used rue in holy water sprinklers, calling it the 'herb of grace'; it appears on the Lithuanian coat of arms.

RYE.magicalUses: 吉普賽人會在愛情法術中使用黑麥。
RYE.lore: Ergot fungus on rye may have caused the 'bewitchment' symptoms in the Salem witch trials; it contains compounds related to LSD.

SAFFRON.ritualUses: 腓尼基人會將番紅花烤成新月形的蛋糕來吃,以榮耀月亮和生育
SAFFRON.magicalUses: 番紅花會添加在愛情類型，以及那些用來提高您望的香包中。也 用於治療類型的法術,在進行治療儀式前，會以其浸劑當作洗手水。
SAFFRON.lore: The most expensive spice by weight — each crocus flower yields only three tiny stigmas; Cleopatra bathed in saffron-infused water.

SAGE.magicalUses: 鼠尾草一直用來延年益蠹，有時甚至是為了達到永生。做法
SAGE.lore: The Latin name 'Salvia' means 'to save'; an old proverb asks, 'Why should a man die whilst sage grows in his garden?'

SAGEBRUSH.ritualUses: 美國印第安人一直以來會在其儀式中燃燒山艾。
SAGEBRUSH.magicalUses: 用山艾洗澡,来淨化自己過去所有的邪惡和負面行為。
SAGEBRUSH.lore: Sacred to many Native American nations for smudging ceremonies; it defines the landscape of the American West.

ST.JOHN'S.magicalUses: 將聖約翰草穿戴在身上,可以消除發燒和感冒,並讓士兵立於不 敗之地，還能吸引愛情。
ST.JOHN'S.lore: Traditionally gathered on Midsummer's Eve; medieval people hung it over doors to repel evil spirits.

SANDALWOOD,WHITE.magicalUses: 通常會在進行保護、治療和驅魔類型的法術期間,燃燒檀香 粉。與薰衣草混合時,可製作出一種召靈的薰香。
SANDALWOOD,WHITE.lore: Indian sandalwood must grow 30+ years before harvest; temples have burned it for over 4,000 years.

SANDALWOOD,RED.magicalUses: 燃燒紫檀木會带來愛情。
SANDALWOOD,RED.lore: Red sandalwood is not true sandalwood but a legume; prized in Hindu rituals for making paste marks (tilaka) on the forehead.

SANDARAC,GUM.lore: Ancient Egyptians and Romans used sandarac resin as varnish for paintings and manuscripts; it was also burned as temple incense.
SANDARAC,GUM.magicalUses: Burned as incense for protection and purification. The resin is added to protection sachets and used to consecrate magical tools.

SARSAPARILLA.magicalUses: 將菝葜與肉桂、檀香粉混合,撒在營業場所周遭,可招財。它也 用於愛情法術。
SARSAPARILLA.lore: The original flavoring of root beer before sassafras; cowboys in the Old West really did order it at saloons.

SASSAFRAS.magicalUses: 將檫樹放在錢包或皮夾中,可招財;或是將其燒掉,也有同樣的 作用。
SASSAFRAS.lore: The original flavoring of root beer; Spanish explorers carried sassafras back to Europe as a cure-all wonder drug.

SCULLCAP.magicalUses: 美黃芩適用於放鬆和和平類型的法術。穿戴美黃芩的女人,可確 保其丈夫不會受到其他女人的迷惑。
SCULLCAP.lore: Named for the cap-shaped calyx; Native Americans used it as a ceremonial herb for rites of passage.

SENNA.magicalUses: 番瀉葉會用在愛情法術中。
SENNA.lore: Ancient Egyptian physicians recorded senna's use as a laxative in the Ebers Papyrus (c. 1550 BCE), making it one of the oldest known medicines.

SESAME.lore: The phrase 'Open Sesame' from One Thousand and One Nights refers to sesame pods, which burst open when ripe.

SHALLOT.lore: Named after the ancient city of Ashkelon in Israel; Crusaders brought them back to Europe.
SHALLOT.magicalUses: Used similarly to onion in purification and protection. Hung in the kitchen to absorb negative energy.

SKUNK.magicalUses: 將紅蔥頭加入洗澡水中,可治療不幸。
SKUNK.lore: Named for the pungent smell of its crushed leaves; Native Americans used it medicinally despite the odor.

SLIPPERY.magicalUses: 燃燒北美滑榆樹,然後將一個打結的黃色繩索或線丢入這火 中，可平息任何針對你的間話。
SLIPPERY.lore: During the American Revolution, soldiers survived on slippery elm bark when food was scarce.

SLOE.magicalUses: 掛在門口或隨身攜帶黑刺李,可驅散邪惡和災難,消除惡魔和負 面振動的能量。
SLOE.lore: Sloe berries flavor sloe gin, a British country tradition; the blackthorn's dense thorns made it the preferred wood for Irish shillelagh walking sticks.

SNAKEROOT.magicalUses: 這種藥草的根可當作好運護身符，也用來破除詛咒和咒語。傳説 也會指引財路。
SNAKEROOT.lore: Used by Native Americans for snakebite; Abraham Lincoln's mother reportedly died from milk sickness caused by cattle eating white snakeroot.

SNAPDRAGON.magicalUses: 在身上佩戴金鱼草的任何一部分，都能阻止他人欺騙你。在脖子
SNAPDRAGON.lore: Children squeeze the flower to make the 'dragon's mouth' open and close; medieval Europeans believed them to be protection against curses.

SOLOMON'S.magicalUses: 将其根部放在房子的四個角落，具有保護作用；用來進行各類型
SOLOMON'S.lore: Named because the root scar resembles King Solomon's mystical sigil; used in Chinese medicine for over 2,000 years.

SORREL,WOOD.magicalUses: 隨身攜帶白花酢漿草(乾燥)的葉子,可以保護心臟免受疾病侵
SORREL,WOOD.lore: Wood sorrel (shamrock-shaped) may be the true Irish shamrock St. Patrick used — the debate between it and clover continues to this day.

SOUTHERNWOOD.magicalUses: 青蒿用於爱情法術,可攜帶或放置在臥室內。有時會將鹼蒿放在 床下,用以引發慾望。
SOUTHERNWOOD.lore: Called 'lad's love' in English folk tradition because young men once used it in courtship bouquets; its French name means 'citrus-scented.'

SPANISH.magicalUses: 將西班牙苔蘚種在房子上或家 禅，具有保護作用。
SPANISH.lore: Not a moss but a bromeliad; used by Native Americans and colonists to stuff mattresses and insulate buildings.

SPEARMINT.magicalUses: 綠薄荷應用於所有治療型類的魔法，尤其是肺部疾病。 綠薄荷有時也會用來挑起慾望。聞綠薄荷可增加並強化心智能力。 睡覺時使用以綠薄荷填充的枕頭或床墊,會得到保護。
SPEARMINT.lore: In Greek myth, Minthe was turned into spearmint by jealous Persephone; Romans used it to scent bathwater and freshen banquet halls.

SPIDERWORT.lore: Named because its sap turns stringy like a spider's web; modern scientists use spiderwort cells to detect radiation — they turn pink when exposed.
SPIDERWORT.magicalUses: Spiderwort is carried for love and used in spells to attract a lover.

SPIKENARD.magicalUses: 美國達科塔州( Dakota) 的印第安 人會攜帶紫露草來吸引愛情。
SPIKENARD.lore: Mary Magdalene anointed Jesus's feet with costly spikenard oil; it was imported from the Himalayas to the ancient Mediterranean.

SQUILL.magicalUses: 自古以來,海蔥就一直用於魔法。要保護居家環境,可在窗戶上 掛一顆海蔥。將一顆海蔥放入罐子或盒子中,再加入幾個銀幣,可招財。
SQUILL.lore: Ancient Egyptians hung squill bulbs over doorways for protection; Greek physicians prescribed it for heart conditions.

STAR.magicalUses: 八角的種子可當成薰香來燒,藉此增加靈力，佩戴以其所製作的 珠子，也有同様的效果。
STAR.lore: A key spice in Chinese five-spice powder and Vietnamese pho; the industrial source of shikimic acid for Tamiflu.

STILLENGIA.magicalUses: 燃燒其根部能發展靈力。
STILLENGIA.lore: Used by Native Americans of the Southeast as a blood cleanser; early American herbalists called it 'queen's root.'

STRAW.magicalUses: 稻草會帶來幸運,因此常會用 小袋子攜带。
STRAW.lore: Ancient farmers practiced 'corn dolly' traditions — weaving the last sheaf of straw into figures to house the grain spirit until spring.

STRAWBERRY.magicalUses: 草莓是一種愛的食物,攜帶草莓葉會有好運。
STRAWBERRY.lore: In Norse mythology, strawberries are sacred to Frigga; medieval stonemasons carved strawberry motifs on altars as symbols of perfection.

SUGAR.magicalUses: 糖一直是用於調配爱情和慾望魔藥。所以,不妨一邊吃甘蔗,一 邊想你的愛人。
SUGAR.lore: First domesticated in New Guinea 10,000 years ago; sugar drove the colonial slave trade and reshaped world history.

SUMBUL.magicalUses: 要吸引爱情,可攜帶驚香阿魏,或是當成薰香燃燒,或是將其浸 劑加在浴缸中。要確保效果良好，[上述三]種方法可以同時進行。
SUMBUL.lore: Also called 'musk root' for its musky fragrance; Central Asian traditional healers used it as a nerve tonic.

SUNFLOWER.magicalUses: 想要懷孕的女性會吃向日葵籽。要保護自己避免染上天花,可將 葵花籽放在脖子上，可放在一個袋子中，或是像珠子一様串起來。
SUNFLOWER.lore: The Incas worshipped sunflowers as images of their sun god; each flower head can contain up to 2,000 seeds arranged in Fibonacci spirals.

SWEETGRASS.lore: One of the four sacred plants in many Native American traditions; its braided form represents mind, body, and spirit.
SWEETGRASS.magicalUses: Burned as a purification smudge and to attract positive energies. Often braided and used in Native American ceremonies to call spirits and bless sacred space.

SWEETPEA.magicalUses: 在進行法術前燃燒茅香，可引來善 靈或良善的生靈。
SWEETPEA.lore: One of four sacred plants in many Native American traditions; its braided form represents mind, body, and spirit.

TAMARIND.lore: Used in Indian cuisine for thousands of years; ancient Egyptians and Greeks also knew it as a refreshing drink ingredient.
TAMARIND.magicalUses: Used in love spells and sachets. The fruit is carried to attract romance.

TAMARISK.magicalUses: 攜帶羅望子,可以吸引爱情。
TAMARISK.lore: Ancient Persians called it the 'blessed tree'; it appears in the Bible as the tree Abraham planted at Beersheba.

TANSY.magicalUses: 在鞋子中放一點菊蒿，有助於治療持續的發燒。
TANSY.lore: Ancient Greeks placed tansy in coffins to preserve the dead; Charlemagne ordered it grown in all monastery gardens.

TEA.magicalUses: 燃燒茶葉可以確保未來的財富，一般會将茶葉添加到所有金錢類 型的混合藥草和香包中。
TEA.lore: Chinese legend says Emperor Shen Nung discovered tea in 2737 BCE when leaves blew into his hot water.

THISTLE.magicalUses: 將一碗薊放在房間裡,可以強化 精神，恢復房内所有人的活力。
THISTLE.lore: Scotland's national emblem since a Norse raider stepped barefoot on one, alerting sleeping Scots to the invasion.

THISTLE,HOLY.magicalUses: 穿上聖薊,可以保護自己免受邪惡影響,並可加入淨化類型的沐 浴中。神聖的蓟也用於破除咒語的法術。
THISTLE,HOLY.lore: Sacred thistle has been used in European folk medicine since the Middle Ages as a cure-all tonic.

THISTLE,MILK.magicalUses: 盎格魯撒克遜人記錄過一個實例,如果將奶薊掛在男人的脖子
THISTLE,MILK.lore: Ancient Romans believed milk thistle got its white-veined leaves from drops of the Virgin Mary's milk; modern medicine extracts silymarin from it for liver health.

THYME.magicalUses: 燃烧百里香可带來良好的健康,也會基於此目的而穿戴在身 上。它也會用於治療類型的法術中。
THYME.lore: In medieval Europe, ladies embroidered thyme on knights' scarves for courage; the ancient Greeks burned it as temple incense.

TOADFLAX.lore: Named because its flower resembles a toad's mouth; Welsh farmers hung it in stables to protect livestock from hexes.
TOADFLAX.magicalUses: Carried as a protective amulet. Used to break hexes and return negative magic to the sender.

TOADSTOOL.magicalUses: 新疆柳穿魚可以用來當作護身符,以抵禦邪惡,還可以用於破除 咒語。
TOADSTOOL.lore: The word 'toadstool' may come from the German 'Todesstuhl' (death's stool) or the belief that toads sat on them.

TOBACCO.ritualUses: 想要進入蕯滿教的人必須喝下菸草汁,來誘導出幻象,這是他們 訓練的一部分。長久以來,一些美洲印第安人會在宗教儀式中使用草。實 際上，多數人仍然認為這種植物是神聖的。
TOBACCO.magicalUses: 南美洲的印第安人會吸食草，以便和神靈交流。 一開始搭船過
TOBACCO.lore: Sacred to Native American peoples for millennia, used in prayer and ceremony; the Mayans depicted tobacco-smoking gods in temple art.

TOMATO.magicalUses: 在地幔上放一大顆紅番茄,能為家庭帶來繁榮。但需每三天更換 一次 。
TOMATO.lore: Europeans feared tomatoes for 200 years, calling them 'poison apples' — likely because acidic tomato juice leached lead from pewter plates.

TONKA.magicalUses: 會放在愛情類型的香包和混合藥草中，用來吸引愛情。
TONKA.lore: Venezuelan Kariña people have used tonka beans in ceremony for centuries; its sweet coumarin scent is the secret heart of many classic perfumes.

TORMENTIL.magicalUses: 喝下洋委陵菜的浸劑,能夠獲得保護,若是将其拿給愛人喝，可 以維持愛情。靈媒也會飲用這種浸劑,以避免遭到靈魂的永久附身。
TORMENTIL.lore: Used since Viking times to tan leather and treat stomach ailments; the name reflects its power to 'torment' pain.

TRAGACANTH.magicalUses: 紫雲英樹膠可用來將虛無飄渺之物帶入夢境或潛意識深處,只要
TRAGACANTH.lore: Harvested from thorny shrubs in the Middle East for over 3,000 years; ancient Egyptians used this natural gum in embalming and as a pharmaceutical binder.

TRILLIUM.magicalUses: 攜帶延齡草,可吸引錢財和運氣。
TRILLIUM.lore: Sacred to many Native American peoples; it takes seven years for a trillium seed to produce its first flower — a lesson in patience.

TULIP.magicalUses: 鬱金香可用於對抗一般的貧困和惡劣運氣。
TULIP.lore: Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of 1637 was history's first recorded speculative bubble; single bulbs sold for more than houses.

TURMERIC.magicalUses: 長期以來,薑黄一直被用於夏威夷 魔法中的淨化;將鹽水和薑黃混合在一起,然 後灑在需要淨化的區域，有時還會加入一片薑 黄葉子。
TURMERIC.lore: Used in Ayurvedic medicine for over 4,000 years; brides in Hindu wedding ceremonies are anointed with turmeric paste for purification and beauty.

TURNIP.ritualUses: 過去在蕯溫節(十月三十一日)會將蕪菁挖空,在裡面點燃蠟 燭。攜帶這些蕪菁燈籠,或是將其放在窗前,能嚇走惡靈。
TURNIP.magicalUses: 若是無法说服仰慕者放下你,可以在他或她面前放一盤蕪菁,他 們就會明白你的想法。
TURNIP.lore: Before pumpkins, the Irish carved turnips into jack-o'-lanterns for Samhain to ward off evil spirits.

UVA.lore: Called 'bearberry' because bears love the fruit; Native Americans mixed it with tobacco in 'kinnikinnick' smoking blends used in peace pipe ceremonies.
UVA.magicalUses: Used in sachets to increase psychic powers. The leaves are added to divination incenses.

VALERIAN.magicalUses: 将熊果添加到香包中，可以增加靈力。
VALERIAN.lore: Legend says the Pied Piper of Hamelin lured rats with valerian; its name may come from Latin 'valere' — to be strong.

VANILLA.magicalUses: 香荚蘭是一種發酵的蘭花，用於愛情類型的香包；其香味和味 道,據信會誘發慾望。將香莢蘭果實放在一碗糖中,會使其充滿愛的能量振 動,之後可以用這種糖來增甜愛情魔藥的浸劑。
VANILLA.lore: The Totonac people of Mexico first cultivated vanilla; only a specific bee native to Central America originally pollinated it.

VENUS'FLYTRAP.magicalUses: 這些迷人的食蟲植物現在可以在苗圃買到，並且郵寄到府。雖然
VENUS'FLYTRAP.lore: Darwin called it 'the most wonderful plant in the world'; native only to a small area near Wilmington, North Carolina.

VERVAIN.ritualUses: 古羅馬的祭司會用馬鞭草來清理眾神之王朱庇特的祭壇,他們通 常是將一小綑的馬鞭草排放好,來清理祭壇。根據傳統,首先做出這種清理 方式的德魯伊的女兒,她們都帶著馬鞭草做的頭冠;這是代表階級的一種標 誌(就跟任何與「德魯伊教派」有關的東西一樣,必須將此看成是一種詩意 的呈現,而不是歷史事實)。
VERVAIN.magicalUses: 傳統上,要在仲夏之日或是天狼星上升、且太陽和月亮都没有出 現的日子採集馬鞭草，但這並非必要。
VERVAIN.lore: The Romans called it 'herba sacra' (sacred herb); legend says it was used to stanch Christ's wounds on Calvary.

VETCH.magicalUses: 若是你的愛人誤入歧途，拿野豌豆 的根在自己的身上擦拭，然後用布包起來,放 在枕頭下。這能夠提醒他或她，你還在身邊, 並等待著。
VETCH.lore: An ancient nitrogen-fixing crop; Roman farmers planted vetch to restore soil fertility — an early form of sustainable agriculture.

VETIVERT.magicalUses: 燃燒岩蘭草可破解邪惡的法術。
VETIVERT.lore: Called 'khus' in India, where vetiver roots have scented water and woven into cooling screens for centuries.

VIOLET.magicalUses: 攜帶其鮮花能夠抵禦「邪惡的靈體」,並帶來運氣和財富的變 化。與薰衣草混合,會成為一種強大的爱情興奮劑,也能唤起慾望。
VIOLET.lore: Napoleon's supporters used the violet as their secret symbol; Athens was called the 'violet-crowned city' by the poet Pindar.

WAHOO.magicalUses: 取其樹皮製作浸劑,放冷。擦在遭到詛咒的人(或自己)的額頭 上 ，然後説七次「美衛矛」 ( Wahoo) (有些人説，應該用這浸劑畫一個十 字架),這會打破所有針對此人的咒語。
WAHOO.lore: Named from a Dakota word; the bark's shocking pink fruit capsules open to reveal bright orange seeds in autumn.

WALNUT.ritualUses: 在義大利，女巫舉行秘密儀式時, 會在核桃樹下跳舞。
WALNUT.magicalUses: 攜帶核桃在身上,可以強化心臟,防止風濕痛。但是,它們也會
WALNUT.lore: In Roman times, walnuts were thrown at weddings for fertility; the genus name 'Juglans' means 'Jupiter's nuts.'

WAX.magicalUses: 將毬蘭種植在臥室和房子中,可獲得保護。將其星形花乾燥,可
WAX.lore: Colonial Americans made fragrant bayberry (wax myrtle) candles; folk tradition says burning one on Christmas Eve brings prosperity in the new year.

WHEAT.magicalUses: 小麥是豐收的象徵,有時會攜帶在身上或食用,以促進生育和受
WHEAT.lore: The domestication of wheat around 10,000 years ago in the Fertile Crescent is considered the start of civilization itself.

WILLOW.ritualUses: 在英國,沼澤和湖泊附近的埋葬土墩通常種有成排的柳樹,可能 是因為它與死亡的象徵有所聯結的緣故。
WILLOW.magicalUses: 隨身攜帶柳樹葉子,或是用在混合藥草中,可吸引愛情。柳木則 可用來製作専門用於月亮魔法的魔杖。
WILLOW.lore: The original source of aspirin — the bark contains salicin; weeping willows were sacred to the moon goddess across many cultures.

WINTERGREEN.magicalUses: 將白珠樹的葉子放在兒童枕頭中,能夠保護他們,並帶給他們一 生的好運。
WINTERGREEN.lore: During the American Revolution, colonists brewed wintergreen tea as a substitute for taxed British tea.

WINTER'S.lore: Sacred to the Mapuche people of Chile as the 'canelo' — a tree of wisdom, peace, and healing. Captain John Winter used its vitamin C-rich bark to cure scurvy on Sir Francis Drake's 1578 voyage.
WINTER'S.magicalUses: The bark is burned for good luck and used in sachets for love and protection.

WITCH.magicalUses: 攜帶或燃燒冬木樹皮,能確保所有的事業成功。
WITCH.lore: Called 'couch grass' in Britain; its incredibly tenacious roots symbolize persistence in folk magic.

WOLF'S.magicalUses: 烏頭可加到保護類型的香包中,特别適合用來抵禦吸血鬼和狼 人，然而狼人也會用烏頭來自我治療。
WOLF'S.lore: Also called wolfsbane/aconite; medieval legend says it grew from the saliva of the three-headed dog Cerberus.

WOOD.magicalUses: 攜帶木玫瑰可吸引好運和財富。 放在家裡,也可確保好運來。
WOOD.lore: Hawaiian baby woodrose seeds contain LSA; the flower is a symbol of the Hawaiian Islands.

WOODRUFF.magicalUses: 燃燒香豬殃殃,能夠招財和發達,也可以為運動員和戰士帶來最 後的勝利。
WOODRUFF.lore: Sweet woodruff's coumarin scent intensifies when dried; German May wine (Maibowle) has been flavored with it since medieval times.

WORMWOOD.magicalUses: 在薰香中燃燒苦艾，有助於發展靈力，穿戴在身上也有一様的 效果。攜帶苦艾,不僅可以防止遭法術迷惑,也可以避免被海蛇咬傷。此 外，根據古老的傳統,這能抵消毒芹和毒蕈的毒素，但我不會拿自己的生命 來測試其有效性。
WORMWOOD.lore: The key ingredient in absinthe, the 'Green Fairy' that fueled the creativity of Van Gogh, Rimbaud, and bohemian Paris.

YARROW.magicalUses: 西洋蓍草會保護其佩戴者，握在手中時,所有的恐懼都會消 失，並獲得勇氣。
YARROW.lore: Named 'Achillea' because Achilles used it to heal his soldiers' wounds at Troy; Chinese sages use yarrow stalks for I Ching divination.

YELLOW.magicalUses: 美洲印第安人會拿這種植物來摩擦他們的軟皮鞋面和身體,以期
YELLOW.lore: Evening primrose opens its flowers at dusk, earning the folk name 'night candle'; its seed oil is rich in gamma-linolenic acid.

YERBA.magicalUses: 穿戴在身上,可以吸引異性。其浸劑是一種很好的「慾望」魔 藥 ,若是和愛人一 起飲用，能夠確保你們繼續在一起。要切斷彼此關係，則 将一些浸劑灑在地上。
YERBA.lore: Spanish missionaries named it 'holy herb' after learning its medicinal uses from California's indigenous peoples.

YEW.magicalUses: 這種有毒植物有時會用在讓死者復 活的法術中。
YEW.lore: Some European yew trees are over 2,000 years old; pre-Christian peoples planted them in sacred groves as symbols of death and eternal life.

YOHIMBE.lore: Traditional aphrodisiac of West African peoples for centuries; its bark contains yohimbine, one of the few herbal compounds validated by modern pharmacology.
YOHIMBE.magicalUses: Yohimbe bark is used in love and lust spells. It is considered a powerful aphrodisiac in both magical and herbal traditions.

YUCCA.magicalUses: 根據美國印第安人的魔法，如果一個人穿過王蘭纖維所作成的 圈，就會變形成動物。另一種方法是，在魔法師頭上放置一小束王蘭纖 維,這讓他能燮成任何想要的形式。
YUCCA.lore: Southwestern Native Americans used yucca fibers for sandals, rope, and baskets; its root produces a natural soap still used today.
